title: A とか B とか
short_explanation: Used to express multiple examples or possibilities; 'such as', 'like', 'for example'.
long_explanation: The とか grammar point is used to list multiple examples or possibilities. It can be translated as 'such as', 'like', or 'for example' in English. とか is used between the listed items and expresses that the list is not exhaustive.
formation: Noun + とか + Noun + とか

examples.jp: 週末は映画とか買い物とか楽しいことをしたいです。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu wa eiga toka kaimono toka tanoshii koto o shitai desu.
examples.en: I want to do fun things like watching movies and shopping on the weekend.
examples.promptEn: State that on the weekend, you want to do fun things like watching movies or going shopping using listing 〜とか〜とか

examples.jp: 彼女は英語とかフランス語とかいろいろな言葉を話せます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo toka furansugo toka iroirona kotoba o hanasemasu.
examples.en: She can speak various languages, like English and French.
examples.promptEn: State that she can speak various languages, such as English and French using listing 〜とか〜とか

examples.jp: この店は寿司とか刺身とか日本料理を提供しています。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa sushi toka sashimi toka nihon ryouri o teikyou shiteimasu.
examples.en: This restaurant offers Japanese dishes such as sushi and sashimi.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant serves sushi, sashimi, and other Japanese dishes using listing 〜とか〜とか

examples.jp: $1BOXとか$5BOXとか、異なる価格のランチBOXがあります。
examples.romaji: Ichi-doru BOX toka go-doru BOX toka, kotonaru kakaku no ranchi BOX ga arimasu.
examples.en: There are lunch boxes with different prices, like $1 boxes and $5 boxes.
examples.promptEn: State that there are lunch boxes at different price points, such as the $1 box and the $5 box using listing 〜とか〜とか

title: A は B ほど～ありません (A wa B hodo ～ arimasen)
short_explanation: Express that A is not as much as B; 'not as... as', 'not... to the extent of'.
long_explanation: The は B ほど～ありません grammar point is used to express that A is not as much as B or not to the same extent as B, emphasizing the difference. It can be translated as 'not as... as' or 'not... to the extent of' in English.
formation: A は B ほど Verb/adjective ありません

examples.jp: 今日は昨日ほど寒くありません。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa kinou hodo samuku arimasen.
examples.en: Today is not as cold as yesterday.
examples.promptEn: State that it's not as cold today as it was yesterday using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ありません

examples.jp: 彼は私ほど上手に英語を話せません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa watashi hodo jouzu ni eigo o hanasemasen.
examples.en: He cannot speak English as well as I can.
examples.promptEn: State that he doesn't speak English as well as you do using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ありません

examples.jp: このレストランはあのレストランほど高くありません。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran wa ano resutoran hodo takaku arimasen.
examples.en: This restaurant is not as expensive as that restaurant.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant isn't as expensive as that one using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ありません

examples.jp: 彼女は彼ほど忙しくありません。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kare hodo isogashiku arimasen.
examples.en: She is not as busy as him.
examples.promptEn: State that she isn't as busy as he is using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ありません

title: A は B ほど～ない (A wa B hodo ~ nai)
short_explanation: Expressing that A is not as ~ as B; 'not as...as'
long_explanation: The A は B ほど～ない grammar point is used to express that A is not as ~ as B in some aspect. It can be translated as 'not as...as' in English. This structure is commonly used with い-adjectives (without い) and な-adjective. For verbs, you can use the negative potential form.
formation: A は B ほど + い-Adjective stem (without い) + くない, な-Adjective + じゃない, Verb-negative potential form

examples.jp: 山田さんは鈴木さんほど背が高くない。
examples.romaji: Yamada-san wa Suzuki-san hodo se ga takakunai.
examples.en: Yamada is not as tall as Suzuki.
examples.promptEn: State that mr. Yamada isn't as tall as Mr. Suzuki using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ない

examples.jp: このリンゴはあのリンゴほど甘くない。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo wa ano ringo hodo amakunai.
examples.en: This apple is not as sweet as that apple.
examples.promptEn: State that this apple isn't as sweet as that one using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ない

examples.jp: 彼は私ほど勉強ができない。
examples.romaji: Kare wa watashi hodo benkyou ga dekinai.
examples.en: He can't study as well as I can.
examples.promptEn: State that he isn't as good at studying as you are using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ない

examples.jp: このレストランはあのレストランほど静かじゃない。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran wa ano resutoran hodo shizuka janai.
examples.en: This restaurant is not as quiet as that restaurant.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant isn't as quiet as that one using negative comparison 〜は〜ほど～ない

title: A より B のほうが〜 (A yori B no hou ga 〜)
short_explanation: Comparing two things; 'B is more ~ than A'.
long_explanation: The より and のほうが grammar pattern is used to compare two things by means of an adjective or verb. In this structure, item A is compared to item B, suggesting that item B is more ~ than item A.
formation: A + より + B + のほうが + Adjective/Verb

examples.jp: 田中さんより鈴木さんのほうが背が高いです。
examples.romaji: Tanaka-san yori Suzuki-san no hou ga se ga takai desu.
examples.en: Suzuki is taller than Tanaka.
examples.promptEn: State that suzuki is taller than Tanaka using comparative 〜より〜のほうが〜

examples.jp: リンゴよりバナナのほうが甘いです。
examples.romaji: Ringo yori banana no hou ga amai desu.
examples.en: Bananas are sweeter than apples.
examples.promptEn: State that bananas are sweeter than apples using comparative 〜より〜のほうが〜

examples.jp: 冬より夏のほうが暑いです。
examples.romaji: Fuyu yori natsu no hou ga atsui desu.
examples.en: Summer is hotter than winter.
examples.promptEn: State that summer is hotter than winter using comparative 〜より〜のほうが〜

examples.jp: 東京より京都のほうが歴史があると思います。
examples.romaji: Toukyou yori Kyouto no hou ga rekishi ga aru to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think Kyoto has more history than Tokyo.
examples.promptEn: State that you think Kyoto has a longer history than Tokyo using comparative 〜より〜のほうが〜

title: い-Adjective く する/なる (i-Adjective kusuru/naru)
short_explanation: Express a change happening or making something change.
long_explanation: The い-Adjective く する/なる grammar point is used to indicate a change happening (naru) or intentionally making something change (suru). When using this grammatical structure, the い-adjective is changed to its く form, and then is followed by either する (to make the change) or なる (the change happens).
formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + く + する/なる

examples.jp: 部屋を明るくします。
examples.romaji: Heya o akaruku shimasu.
examples.en: I will make the room brighter.
examples.promptEn: State that you will turn on the lights in the room using change of state 〜くする/なる

examples.jp: 彼の顔は赤くなりました。
examples.romaji: Kare no kao wa akaku narimashita.
examples.en: His face turned red.
examples.promptEn: State that his face turned red using change of state 〜くする/なる

examples.jp: この料理を辛くしてください。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri o karaku shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please make this dish spicy.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to make this dish spicy using change of state 〜くする/なる

examples.jp: 雨が降ると、道が滑りやすくなります。
examples.romaji: Ame ga furu to, michi ga suberiyasuku narimasu.
examples.en: When it rains, the road becomes slippery.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when it rains, the roads become slippery using change of state 〜くする/なる

title: な-adjective に する/なる
short_explanation: Used to indicate change or decision; 'to become' or 'to make' with na-adjectives.
long_explanation: The な-adjective に する/なる grammar point is used to express a change or a decision related to a na-adjective. The なる (naru) form indicates a change that occurs by itself, while the する (suru) form indicates a conscious decision made by someone.
formation: な-Adjective + に + する/なる

examples.jp: 部屋をきれいにする。
examples.romaji: Heya o kirei ni suru.
examples.en: To make the room clean.
examples.promptEn: State that clean the room using change of state 〜にする/なる

examples.jp: 彼は元気になりました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa genki ni narimashita.
examples.en: He became energetic.
examples.promptEn: State that he has recovered using change of state 〜にする/なる

examples.jp: 毎日静かにすることが大切です。
examples.romaji: Mainichi shizuka ni suru koto ga taisetsu desu.
examples.en: It is important to make it quiet every day.
examples.promptEn: State that it's important to stay quiet every day using change of state 〜にする/なる

examples.jp: 日本語の勉強が楽しくなるように努力します。
examples.romaji: Nihongo no benkyou ga tanoshiku naru you ni doryoku shimasu.
examples.en: I will try to make studying Japanese become enjoyable.
examples.promptEn: State that you will do your best to make learning Japanese fun using change of state 〜にする/なる

title: Noun しか～ない (Noun shika~nai)
short_explanation: Expresses 'only', 'nothing but', or 'no other'.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun しか～ない is used to emphasize the small quantity or exclusiveness of something. It can be translated as 'only', 'nothing but', or 'no other' in English. It is used with a negative verb to convey the meaning.

examples.jp: 私はリンゴしか食べない。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa ringo shika tabenai.
examples.en: I eat only apples.
examples.promptEn: State that you only eat apples using contrast 〜しか～ない

examples.jp: 電車で行くしかないです。
examples.romaji: Densha de iku shika nai desu.
examples.en: There is no other way but to go by train.
examples.promptEn: State that you have no choice but to take the train using contrast 〜しか～ない

examples.jp: 彼は一冊の本しか持っていない。
examples.romaji: Kare wa isatsu no hon shika motte inai.
examples.en: He has only one book.
examples.promptEn: State that he has only one book using contrast 〜しか～ない

examples.jp: この店にはビールしかない。
examples.romaji: Kono mise ni wa biiru shika nai.
examples.en: There is nothing but beer in this store.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant only serves beer using contrast 〜しか～ない

title: Noun に する (Noun ni suru)
short_explanation: Used to indicate a choice or decision, 'to decide on' or 'to choose'.
long_explanation: The grammar point 'Noun に する' is used to express making a choice or decision, which can be translated as 'to decide on' or 'to choose' in English. It is often used when deciding between different options or making a decision in various situations, such as choosing a menu item, deciding on a plan, or selecting a gift.

examples.jp: メニューからピザにしました。
examples.romaji: Menyu kara piza ni shimashita.
examples.en: I decided on pizza from the menu.
examples.promptEn: State that you chose pizza from the menu using change of state 〜にする

examples.jp: 誕生日プレゼントに時計にするつもりです。
examples.romaji: Tanjoubi purezento ni tokei ni suru tsumori desu.
examples.en: I plan to choose a watch as a birthday present.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to get a watch as a birthday present using change of state 〜にする

examples.jp: 今日の午後は買い物にすることにしました。
examples.romaji: Kyou no gogo wa kaimono ni suru koto ni shimashita.
examples.en: I decided to go shopping this afternoon.
examples.promptEn: State that you decided to go shopping this afternoon using change of state 〜にする

examples.jp: 海外旅行の目的地として、日本にする。
examples.romaji: Kaigai ryokou no mokutekichi toshite, Nihon ni suru.
examples.en: I will choose Japan as the destination for my overseas trip.
examples.promptEn: State that choose Japan as your overseas travel destination using change of state 〜にする

title: Noun に なる (Noun ni naru)
short_explanation: To become; to change into; to turn into.
long_explanation: The 'Noun に なる' grammar point is used to show a change or a transformation from one state or form into another. In English, it can be translated as 'to become', 'to change into', or 'to turn into'. It is often used with nouns that indicate profession, status, or condition.

examples.jp: 彼は医者になりました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa isha ni narimashita.
examples.en: He became a doctor.
examples.promptEn: State that he became a doctor using change of state 〜になる

examples.jp: 子供の頃、私は先生になりたかったです。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no koro, watashi wa sensei ni naritakatta desu.
examples.en: When I was a child, I wanted to become a teacher.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you was a child, you wanted to be a teacher using change of state 〜になる

examples.jp: 彼女は緊張して顔が赤くなりました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kinchou shite kao ga akaku narimashita.
examples.en: She got nervous, and her face turned red.
examples.promptEn: State that she blushed because she was nervous using change of state 〜になる

examples.jp: 春になると桜が咲きます。
examples.romaji: Haru ni naru to sakura ga sakimasu.
examples.en: When it becomes spring, cherry blossoms bloom.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom using change of state 〜になる

title: のために (no tame ni)
short_explanation: Used to express purpose or reason; 'for', 'for the sake of', 'in order to'.
long_explanation: The のために grammar point is used to express the purpose or reason for doing something, or for the benefit of someone or something. It can be translated as 'for', 'for the sake of', or 'in order to' in English. The formation is straightforward, simply place のために after a noun.

examples.jp: 勉強のために、図書館で静かな場所を探しています。
examples.romaji: Benkyou no tame ni, toshokan de shizukana basho o sagashiteimasu.
examples.en: In order to study, I am looking for a quiet place in the library.
examples.promptEn: State that you are looking for a quiet spot in the library to study using reason 〜のために

examples.jp: 彼は家族のために、一生懸命働いています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kazoku no tame ni, isshoukenmei hataraiteimasu.
examples.en: He works hard for the sake of his family.
examples.promptEn: State that he works very hard for his family using reason 〜のために

examples.jp: 健康のために、毎日運動をしています。
examples.romaji: Kenkou no tame ni, mainichi undou o shiteimasu.
examples.en: I exercise every day for the sake of my health.
examples.promptEn: State that you exercise every day to stay healthy using reason 〜のために

examples.jp: 世界平和のために、みんなで協力しましょう。
examples.romaji: Sekai heiwa no tame ni, minna de kyouryoku shimashou.
examples.en: Let's all cooperate for the sake of world peace.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you all work together for world peace using reason 〜のために

title: Noun の 間に (〜no aida ni)
short_explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'during' a specific period or time.
long_explanation: The Noun の 間に grammar point is used to indicate a specific period or time during which an action takes place. It is often translated as 'while' or 'during' in English. This grammar point requires a noun to represent the time or period.

examples.jp: 昼休みの間に銀行に行きます。
examples.romaji: Hiruyasumi no aida ni ginkou ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the bank during lunch break.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the bank during your lunch break using simultaneous action 〜の間に

examples.jp: 夏休みの間に海外旅行に行く予定です。
examples.romaji: Natsuyasumi no aida ni kaigai ryokou ni iku yotei desu.
examples.en: I plan to go on an overseas trip during the summer vacation.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to travel abroad during summer vacation using simultaneous action 〜の間に

examples.jp: 子供たちが学校の間に買い物に行きました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo-tachi ga gakkou no aida ni kaimono ni ikimashita.
examples.en: I went shopping while the kids were at school.
examples.promptEn: State that you went shopping while the children were at school using simultaneous action 〜の間に

examples.jp: 母の日にお母さんにプレゼントを送りました。
examples.romaji: Haha no hi ni okaasan ni purezento o okurimashita.
examples.en: I sent a gift to my mother on Mother’s Day.
examples.promptEn: State that you sent your mom a gift for Mother's Day using simultaneous action 〜の間に

title: Noun ばかり (〜bakari)
short_explanation: Expresses 'only', 'nothing but', 'always', or 'just'.
long_explanation: The ばかり grammar point is used to express that something is only, nothing but, just, or always. It can be attached to nouns, verbs, or adjectives, and has various meanings based on the context.
formation: Noun + ばかり, Verb-casual + ばかり, い-Adjective + ばかり, な-Adjective + だ ばかり

examples.jp: 彼はお金の話ばかりする。
examples.romaji: Kare wa okane no hanashi bakari suru.
examples.en: He talks about nothing but money.
examples.promptEn: State that he talks about nothing but money using contrast 〜ばかり

examples.jp: 彼女は勉強ばかりしている。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa benkyou bakari shiteiru.
examples.en: She is always studying.
examples.promptEn: State that she does nothing but study using contrast 〜ばかり

examples.jp: デパートには高い商品ばかりだ。
examples.romaji: Depaato ni wa takai shouhin bakari da.
examples.en: There are only expensive items in the department store.
examples.promptEn: State that the department store is full of expensive items using contrast 〜ばかり

examples.jp: この部屋は狭いばかりだ。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa semai bakari da.
examples.en: This room is nothing but small.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is just too small using contrast 〜ばかり

title: Noun を あげる (Noun wo ageru)
short_explanation: To give something to someone; 'give', 'offer', 'present'.
long_explanation: The を あげる grammar point is used to express giving something to someone. It can be translated as 'give', 'offer', or 'present' in English. This construction is commonly used with nouns to indicate giving or offering a tangible item, action, or favor to someone else.

examples.jp: プレゼントをあげる。
examples.romaji: Purezento wo ageru.
examples.en: I give a present.
examples.promptEn: State that you are giving a present using giving and receiving 〜をあげる

examples.jp: 友達に花をあげた。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni hana wo ageta.
examples.en: I gave flowers to my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you gave your friend some flowers using giving and receiving 〜をあげる

examples.jp: 父に時計をあげます。
examples.romaji: Chichi ni tokei wo agemasu.
examples.en: I will give a watch to my father.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to give your father a watch using giving and receiving 〜をあげる

examples.jp: 彼女に手紙をあげたい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ni tegami wo agetai.
examples.en: I want to give her a letter.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to give her a letter using giving and receiving 〜をあげる

title: Nounをいただく (Noun wo itadaku)
short_explanation: To receive or accept something politely; 'to receive', 'to get', 'to accept'.
long_explanation: The Nounをいただく grammar point is used to express the action of receiving or accepting something in a polite or humble manner. The verb 'いただく' is a more respectful version of the verb 'もらう' (to receive), so using 'いただく' shows humility and respect towards the person who is giving you something.

examples.jp: プレゼントをいただきありがとうございます。
examples.romaji: Purezento wo itadaki arigatou gozaimasu.
examples.en: Thank you for the gift that I received.
examples.promptEn: State that thank you for the gift using 〜をいただく

examples.jp: 先生からアドバイスをいただきました。
examples.romaji: Sensei kara adobaisu wo itadakimashita.
examples.en: I received advice from my teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you received some advice from your teacher using 〜をいただく

examples.jp: このコーヒーをいただいていいですか？
examples.romaji: Kono koohii wo itadaite ii desu ka?
examples.en: May I have this coffee?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether may you have this coffee using 〜をいただく

examples.jp: 会社の上司に昇進のお知らせをいただきました。
examples.romaji: Kaisha no joushi ni shoushin no oshirase wo itadakimashita.
examples.en: I received a promotion notification from my boss at the company.
examples.promptEn: State that my boss at work told you you have been promoted using 〜をいただく

title: Nounをくださる
short_explanation: Used to express someone doing something as a favor or for the benefit of the speaker.
long_explanation: The grammar point 'Nounをくださる' is a polite expression used to say that someone is giving or doing something for the benefit of the speaker. It is often used when referring to people who have a higher social status or when expressing gratitude for their actions.

examples.jp: 先生が資料をくださった。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga shiryou wo kudasatta.
examples.en: The teacher gave me the materials.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher gave you some handouts using 〜をくださる

examples.jp: お母さんがおやつをくださる。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ga oyatsu wo kudasaru.
examples.en: My mother gives me snacks.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom gives you a snack using 〜をくださる

examples.jp: 上司がアドバイスをくださいました。
examples.romaji: Joushi ga adobaisu wo kudasaimashita.
examples.en: My boss gave me advice.
examples.promptEn: State that my boss gave you some advice using 〜をくださる

examples.jp: 友達がプレゼントをくださった。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga purezento wo kudasatta.
examples.en: My friend gave me a present.
examples.promptEn: State that a friend gave you a present using 〜をくださる

title: Noun を くれる (Noun wo kureru)
short_explanation: Expresses that someone gives a thing to the speaker or someone close to the speaker.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun を くれる is used to express when someone (other than the speaker) gives something to the speaker or someone close to the speaker. The giver is the subject, and the receiver is the speaker or someone close to the speaker. くれる indicates that the action of giving 'favors' the speaker or someone close to the speaker.
formation: Giver + が + Receiver + に + Noun + を + くれる

examples.jp: 友達が私にプレゼントをくれました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi ni purezento wo kuremashita.
examples.en: My friend gave me a present.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend gave you a present using giving and receiving 〜をくれる

examples.jp: 彼が私に花をくれた。
examples.romaji: Kare ga watashi ni hana wo kureta.
examples.en: He gave me flowers.
examples.promptEn: State that he gave you flowers using giving and receiving 〜をくれる

examples.jp: 先生が私に本をくれました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga watashi ni hon wo kuremashita.
examples.en: The teacher gave me a book.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher gave you a book using giving and receiving 〜をくれる

examples.jp: お母さんが弟にお菓子をくれました。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ga otouto ni okashi wo kuremashita.
examples.en: Mom gave my little brother some sweets.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom gave your younger brother some snacks using giving and receiving 〜をくれる

title: Noun を さしあげる (Noun wo sashiageru)
short_explanation: A polite way of expressing to give something.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun を さしあげる is used to say that you are giving something to someone in a polite way. When offering something to a person of higher status, this expression is used. It is used in conjunction with a noun and replaces the regular verb あげる (ageru) to give.
formation: Noun + を + さしあげる

examples.jp: 先生に本をさしあげます。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni hon wo sashiagemasu.
examples.en: I will give a book to the teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you will give the book to the teacher using giving and receiving 〜をさしあげる

examples.jp: お母さんに花をさしあげたいです。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ni hana wo sashiagetai desu.
examples.en: I want to give flowers to my mother.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to give your mom some flowers using giving and receiving 〜をさしあげる

examples.jp: お客様にお茶をさしあげましょう。
examples.romaji: Okyakusama ni ocha wo sashiagemashou.
examples.en: Let's offer tea to the guest.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you offer the customer some tea using giving and receiving 〜をさしあげる

examples.jp: 先輩にプレゼントをさしあげたら、喜んでいました。
examples.romaji: Senpai ni purezento wo sashiagetara, yorokonde imashita.
examples.en: When I gave a present to my senior, they were delighted.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you gave your senior a gift, she was delighted using giving and receiving 〜をさしあげる

title: Noun もらう (Noun wo morau)
short_explanation: To receive or get something from someone; 'to receive', 'to get'.
long_explanation: The もらう (morau) grammar point is used to express the action of receiving or getting something from someone. It usually emphasizes that the action was done for you or you were the beneficiary of the action. The formation requires a noun followed by the particle を (wo) before 'もらう'.

examples.jp: 友達からプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi kara purezento wo moraimashita.
examples.en: I received a gift from my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you received a gift from a friend using giving and receiving 〜もらう

examples.jp: 先生にアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni adobaisu wo moraimashita.
examples.en: I got advice from my teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you received some advice from your teacher using giving and receiving 〜もらう

examples.jp: お父さんからお小遣いをもらう。
examples.romaji: Otousan kara okozukai wo morau.
examples.en: To receive an allowance from one's father.
examples.promptEn: State that you get an allowance from your dad using giving and receiving 〜もらう

examples.jp: 彼女に手紙をもらった。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ni tegami wo moratta.
examples.en: I got a letter from her.
examples.promptEn: State that you received a letter from her using giving and receiving 〜もらう

title: Noun + 中 (Noun + ちゅう)
short_explanation: Express 'in the middle of', 'during', or 'in the process of'.
long_explanation: The 中 (ちゅう) grammar point is used to express that something is in the middle of, during, or in the process of happening. It is attached to a noun to convey this meaning (e.g., 勉強中, 仕事中, 会議中). It is also sometimes read as じゅう depending on the word (e.g., 授業中).

examples.jp: 彼は仕事中です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shigotochuu desu.
examples.en: He is in the middle of work.
examples.promptEn: State that he is at work using 〜中

examples.jp: 試験中、携帯電話を使ってはいけません。
examples.romaji: Shiken chuu, keitai denwa wo tsukatte wa ikemasen.
examples.en: During the exam, you must not use your mobile phone.
examples.promptEn: Warn that it is not allowed to use your cell phone during the exam using 〜中

examples.jp: 映画を観ている最中に、彼は泣き始めました。
examples.romaji: Eiga o mite iru saichuu ni, kare wa naki hajimemashita.
examples.en: In the middle of watching the movie, he started to cry.
examples.promptEn: State that while watching the movie, he started crying using 〜中

examples.jp: 彼女は今勉強中です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa ima benkyouchuu desu.
examples.en: She is currently studying.
examples.promptEn: State that she is studying right now using 〜中

title: Verb させられる (Verb-saserareru)
short_explanation: Express the passive causative form; 'to be made to', 'to be forced to'.
long_explanation: The Verb させられる grammar point is the passive causative form of the verb. It is used to describe a situation where someone or something causes or forces another person to do something. This construction of passive causative is useful to show that the action was not done voluntarily by the person.
formation: Group 1 Verb: Replace ～う with ～わせられる, Group 2 Verb: Replace ～る with ～させられる, Group 3 Verb: する → させられる, くる → こさせられる

examples.jp: 子供たちは先生に宿題をやらせられました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo-tachi wa sensei ni shukudai wo yaraseraremashita.
examples.en: The children were made to do their homework by the teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that the children were made to do their homework by their teacher using passive 〜させられる

examples.jp: 彼は会社にもっと働かせられた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kaisha ni motto hatarakaserareta.
examples.en: He was forced to work more by the company.
examples.promptEn: State that he was made to work harder at the company using passive 〜させられる

examples.jp: 私は友達にその機密を話させられました。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa tomodachi ni sono kimitsu o hanasaseraremashita.
examples.en: I was made to reveal that secret by my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you was forced to tell your friend that secret using passive 〜させられる

examples.jp: 怪我をした選手は、コーチに休ませられました。
examples.romaji: Kega wo shita senshu wa, kouchi ni yasumaseraremashita.
examples.en: The injured player was forced to rest by the coach.
examples.promptEn: State that the injured player was told by the coach to rest using passive 〜させられる

title: Verb させる (Verb-saseru)
short_explanation: Expresses 'to make someone do something', 'to let someone do something', or 'to cause someone to do something'.
long_explanation: The ～させる verb form is used to describe causing or allowing someone to do something. It can be translated as 'to make someone do something', 'to let someone do something', or 'to cause someone to do something' in English. The formation of the ～させる form depends on the verb it is attached to.
formation: Group 1 Verbs: Change the last hiragana to ～せる, Group 2 Verbs: Remove ～る and add ～させる, Group 3 Verbs: する → させる, くる → こさせる

examples.jp: 先生が生徒に宿題をさせました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga seito ni shukudai o sasemashita.
examples.en: The teacher made the students do homework.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher assigned homework to the students using causative 〜させる

examples.jp: 母が私に部屋を掃除させました。
examples.romaji: Haha ga watashi ni heya o souji sasemashita.
examples.en: My mother made me clean my room.
examples.promptEn: State that my mother made you clean your room using causative 〜させる

examples.jp: 彼女にピアノを弾かせてあげました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ni piano o hikasete agemashita.
examples.en: I let her play the piano.
examples.promptEn: State that you let her play the piano using causative 〜させる

examples.jp: 上司は彼にそのプログラムを作らせました。
examples.romaji: Joushi wa kare ni sono puroguramu o tsukurasemashita.
examples.en: The boss made him create the program.
examples.promptEn: State that his boss had him create that program using causative 〜させる

title: Verb た ことがある (Verb ta koto ga aru)
short_explanation: Expresses the experience of having done something in the past.
long_explanation: The ～たことがある grammar point is used to express the experience of having done an action in the past. It indicates that the speaker has had the experience of doing something at least once before. It is formed by adding ことがある to the た-form of the verb.

examples.jp: 日本に行ったことがあります。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni itta koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: I have been to Japan before.
examples.promptEn: State that you have been to Japan using experience 〜たことがある

examples.jp: 寿司を食べたことがありますか？
examples.romaji: Sushi wo tabeta koto ga arimasu ka?
examples.en: Have you ever eaten sushi before?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether have you ever eaten sushi using experience 〜たことがある

examples.jp: 彼はマラソンを走ったことがあります。
examples.romaji: Kare wa marason wo hashitta koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: He has experienced running a marathon.
examples.promptEn: State that he has run a marathon using experience 〜たことがある

examples.jp: 私はスカイダイビングをしたことがありません。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa sukaidaibingu wo shita koto ga arimasen.
examples.en: I have never experienced skydiving.
examples.promptEn: State that you have never gone skydiving using experience 〜たことがある

title: Verb た ときに (Verb た ときに)
short_explanation: Express an action or event that occurred at a specific time in the past; 'when', 'at the time'.
long_explanation: The たときに grammar point is used to express an action that happened at a specific time in the past, usually with a focus on a specific event or moment. It can be translated as 'when' or 'at the time' in English. This grammar point requires a verb in its た-form followed by ときに to indicate the time at which the action occurred.

examples.jp: 映画を見たときに、泣きました。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mita toki ni, nakimashita.
examples.en: When I watched the movie, I cried.
examples.promptEn: State that you cried when you watched the movie using 〜たときに

examples.jp: 彼に初めて会ったときに、遅刻していました。
examples.romaji: Kare ni hajimete atta toki ni, chikoku shite imashita.
examples.en: When I first met him, he was late.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you first met him, he was late using 〜たときに

examples.jp: 日本へ行ったときに、たくさんの写真を撮りました。
examples.romaji: Nihon e itta toki ni, takusan no shashin wo torimashita.
examples.en: When I went to Japan, I took a lot of photos.
examples.promptEn: State that you took a lot of photos when you went to Japan using 〜たときに

examples.jp: 友達が家に来たときに、ゲームをしました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga ie ni kita toki ni, geemu wo shimashita.
examples.en: When my friend came to my house, we played games.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when your friend came over, you played a game using 〜たときに

title: Verb た ところ (Verb ta tokoro)
short_explanation: Expresses the situation right after an action has taken place.
long_explanation: The たところ grammar point is used to describe a situation that occurs right after an action has taken place. It is often translated as 'just now', 'right after', or 'when'. The formation is relatively simple as it only requires the verb in its た form (past tense) followed by ところ.

examples.jp: ドアを開けたところ、猫が飛び出してきた。
examples.romaji: Doa wo aketa tokoro, neko ga tobidashite kita.
examples.en: When I opened the door, a cat came jumping out.
examples.promptEn: State that as soon as you opened the door, a cat darted out using 〜たところ

examples.jp: 電話を切ったところ、また鳴った。
examples.romaji: Denwa wo kitta tokoro, mata natta.
examples.en: Right after I hung up the phone, it rang again.
examples.promptEn: State that you had just hung up the phone when it rang again using 〜たところ

examples.jp: 宿題を終わらせたところで、友達から連絡が来た。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo owaraseta tokoro de, tomodachi kara renraku ga kita.
examples.en: Just as I finished my homework, I got a message from my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that just as you finished your homework, a friend contacted you using 〜たところ

examples.jp: 買い物をして帰ったところ、財布を失くしたことに気づいた。
examples.romaji: Kaimono wo shite kaetta tokoro, saifu wo nakushita koto ni kizuita.
examples.en: After shopping and returning home, I realized I had lost my wallet.
examples.promptEn: State that you had just finished shopping and returned home when you realized you had lost your wallet using 〜たところ

title: Verb たほうがいい (〜ta hou ga ii)
short_explanation: Used to give advice or make a suggestion to someone - 'it's better if...'.
long_explanation: The たほうがいい grammar point is used to give advice or make a suggestion to someone. It can be translated as 'it's better if...', 'should', or 'it's a good idea to'. It is formed by conjugating the verb into the past tense (た-form) and adding ほうがいい.

examples.jp: 早く寝たほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Hayaku neta hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's better if you go to bed early.
examples.promptEn: State that you should go to bed early using comparative 〜たほうがいい

examples.jp: もっと勉強したほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Motto benkyou shita hou ga ii.
examples.en: You should study more.
examples.promptEn: State that you should study more using comparative 〜たほうがいい

examples.jp: 病気の時は、薬を飲んだほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Byouki no toki wa, kusuri wo nonda hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's a good idea to take medicine when you're sick.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you're sick, you should take medicine using comparative 〜たほうがいい

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲まないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo nomanai hou ga ii.
examples.en: It's better if you don't drink coffee.
examples.promptEn: State that you shouldn't drink coffee using comparative 〜たほうがいい

title: Verb ために (tame ni)
short_explanation: Used to describe the purpose or reason for an action; 'for the sake of', 'in order to', 'because of'.
long_explanation: The ために (tame ni) grammar point is used to express either the purpose of doing something (in which case it translates to 'for the sake of' or 'in order to') or the cause/reason for a situation (in which case it translates to 'because of'). Typically, we use the dictionary form of the verb (e.g., 合格する) for the 'in order to' meaning. For an adjective or noun, attach ために appropriately (い-Adjective + ために, な-Adjective + な + ために, Noun + の + ために).
formation:
1) Verb (dictionary form) + ために (purpose)
2) い-Adjective + ために (reason)
3) な-Adjective + な + ために (reason)
4) Noun + の + ために (reason)

examples.jp: 試験に合格するために、毎日勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, mainichi benkyou shiteimasu.
examples.en: I study every day in order to pass the exam.
examples.promptEn: State that you study every day to pass the exam using reason 〜ために

examples.jp: 健康のために、毎日運動しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Kenkou no tame ni, mainichi undou shinakereba narimasen.
examples.en: For the sake of health, I must exercise daily.
examples.promptEn: State that for the sake of your health, you must exercise every day using reason 〜ために

examples.jp: 仕事が忙しいために、友達と会う時間がありません。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga isogashii tame ni, tomodachi to au jikan ga arimasen.
examples.en: Because my work is busy, I don't have time to meet friends.
examples.promptEn: State that you are so busy with work that you don't have time to meet up with your friends using reason 〜ために

examples.jp: 雨が降ったために、試合が中止されました。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futta tame ni, shiai ga chuushi saremashita.
examples.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.
examples.promptEn: State that the game was canceled because it rained using reason 〜ために

title: Verb つもり (〜tsumori)
short_explanation: Express the intention, plan, or determination to do something; 'I intend to', 'I plan to', 'I'm determined to'.
long_explanation: The ～つもり grammar point is used to express the intention, plan, or determination to do something. It can be translated as 'I intend to', 'I plan to', or 'I'm determined to' in English. It is used with verbs in the casual form.

examples.jp: 明日、友達に会うつもりです。
examples.romaji: Ashita, tomodachi ni au tsumori desu.
examples.en: I plan to meet my friend tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to meet your friend tomorrow using intention 〜つもり

examples.jp: 今夜、晩ご飯を作るつもりです。
examples.romaji: Konya, bangohan o tsukuru tsumori desu.
examples.en: I intend to cook dinner tonight.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to make dinner tonight using intention 〜つもり

examples.jp: 来年、留学するつもりです。
examples.romaji: Rainen, ryuugaku suru tsumori desu.
examples.en: I plan to study abroad next year.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to study abroad next year using intention 〜つもり

examples.jp: この週末、山に登るつもりです。
examples.romaji: Kono shuumatsu, yama ni noboru tsumori desu.
examples.en: I'm determined to climb the mountain this weekend.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to go hiking this weekend using intention 〜つもり

title: Verb てあげる (Verb te ageru)
short_explanation: Used to express doing something for someone; 'do something for someone'.
long_explanation: The てあげる grammar point is used to express that the speaker or someone other than the listener is doing something for someone else. It shows that the action is being done as a favor or out of kindness. This grammar point is used with verbs in their て-form, followed by あげる.

examples.jp: 友達が疲れていたから、荷物を持ってあげた。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga tsukareteita kara, nimotsu o motte ageta.
examples.en: Since my friend was tired, I carried their luggage for them.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend was tired, so you carried her bags for her using giving and receiving 〜てあげる

examples.jp: 弟は宿題がわからなかったので、手伝ってあげた。
examples.romaji: Otouto wa shukudai ga wakaranakatta node, tetsudatte ageta.
examples.en: My younger brother couldn't understand the homework, so I helped him.
examples.promptEn: State that my younger brother didn't understand his homework, so you helped him using giving and receiving 〜てあげる

examples.jp: 彼女が遅れそうだったから、駅まで迎えに行ってあげた。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga okuresou datta kara, eki made mukae ni itte ageta.
examples.en: She was running late, so I went to pick her up at the station.
examples.promptEn: State that since she looked like she might be late, you went to pick her up at the station using giving and receiving 〜てあげる

examples.jp: 犬はのどが渇いたそうだったので、水を飲ませてあげた。
examples.romaji: Inu wa nodo ga kawaita sou datta node, mizu o nomasete ageta.
examples.en: The dog seemed thirsty, so I gave it water to drink.
examples.promptEn: State that the dog seemed thirsty, so you gave it some water using giving and receiving 〜てあげる

title: Verb て ある (Verb-te aru)
short_explanation: Indicates that an action has been done and its result is still in effect.
long_explanation: The ～てある grammar point is used to express that an action has been done and its result remains in effect. It indicates that the action was intentionally performed and its effect continues. The formation is done by conjugating the verb into its て-form and then adding ある.

examples.jp: 窓が開けてある。
examples.romaji: Mado ga akete aru.
examples.en: The window has been opened (and remains open).
examples.promptEn: State that the window is open using 〜てある

examples.jp: 宿題がもう終わってある。
examples.romaji: Shukudai ga mou owatte aru.
examples.en: The homework has already been done (and remains that way).
examples.promptEn: State that you have already finished your homework using 〜てある

examples.jp: 洗濯物が全部干してある。
examples.romaji: Sentakumono ga zenbu hoshite aru.
examples.en: The laundry has been hung up to dry (and remains that way).
examples.promptEn: State that all the laundry has been hung out to dry using 〜てある

examples.jp: この部屋はきれいに掃除してある。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa kirei ni souji shite aru.
examples.en: This room has been cleaned (and remains clean).
examples.promptEn: State that this room has been cleaned thoroughly using 〜てある

title: Verb て いく (Verb-te iku)
short_explanation: Expresses an action that continues on into the future or a change that progresses over time.
long_explanation: The て いく grammar point is used to indicate that an action will continue or a change will progress into the future. It can be attached to the て-form of a verb and is often translated as 'to keep', 'to continue', or 'to go on' in English.

examples.jp: このまま練習を続けていくと、上達するでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kono mama renshuu o tsuzukete iku to, joutatsu suru deshou.
examples.en: If you keep practicing like this, you will improve.
examples.promptEn: State that if you keep practicing like this, you'll improve using change of state 〜ていく

examples.jp: 彼は成長していくうちに、自立心が強くなった。
examples.romaji: Kare wa seichou shite iku uchi ni, jiritsushin ga tsuyoku natta.
examples.en: As he grew up, his independence became stronger.
examples.promptEn: State that as he grew up, he became more independent using change of state 〜ていく

examples.jp: この会社はこれからも技術革新を行っていくでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kono kaisha wa korekara mo gijutsu kakushin o okonatte iku deshou.
examples.en: This company will continue to innovate in technology in the future.
examples.promptEn: State that this company will continue to innovate in the future using change of state 〜ていく

examples.jp: 子供たちはどんどん学んでいく。
examples.romaji: Kodomo-tachi wa dondon manande iku.
examples.en: Children will keep learning more and more.
examples.promptEn: State that the children are learning more and more using change of state 〜ていく

title: Verb ていただきたい (te itadakitai)
short_explanation: Express a polite request or desire that someone does something for you.
long_explanation: The ていただきたい grammar point is used to express a polite request or a desire for someone to do something for you. It is formed by attaching いただきたい to the て-form of the verb. It is more polite than the て-form + ほしい construction.
formation: Verb-て form + いただきたい

examples.jp: 資料をコピーしていただきたいです。
examples.romaji: Shiryou wo kopii shite itadakitai desu.
examples.en: I would like you to make copies of the documents.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to you would like you to make copies of the materials using polite request 〜ていただきたい

examples.jp: この仕事を手伝っていただきたいのですが。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wo tetsudatte itadakitai no desu ga.
examples.en: I would like to ask for your assistance with this work.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to you want to ask for your help with this task using polite request 〜ていただきたい

examples.jp: もしよろしければ、指導していただきたいです。
examples.romaji: Moshi yoroshikereba, shidou shite itadakitai desu.
examples.en: If it is not too much trouble, I would like you to guide me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to if you wouldn't mind, you would appreciate some guidance using polite request 〜ていただきたい

examples.jp: 駅まで送っていただきたいんですが。
examples.romaji: Eki made okutte itadakitain desu ga.
examples.en: I was wondering if you could give me a ride to the station.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to you want you to give you a ride to the station using polite request 〜ていただきたい

title: Verb ていただく (〜te itadaku)
short_explanation: Used to express receiving someone's favor or help; 'to kindly do'.
long_explanation: The ～ていただく grammar point is used to express that someone has kindly done a favor or provided help. It is a more polite and humble way of saying that you received someone's help. The formation is created by attaching the て-form of the verb + いただく.

examples.jp: メールを送っていただいて、ありがとうございます。
examples.romaji: Meeru o okutte itadaite, arigatou gozaimasu.
examples.en: Thank you for kindly sending the email.
examples.promptEn: State that thank you for sending you the email using giving and receiving 〜ていただく

examples.jp: 荷物を運んでいただいて、助かりました。
examples.romaji: Nimotsu o hakonde itadaite, tasukarimashita.
examples.en: You really helped me by carrying the luggage.
examples.promptEn: State that thank you for carrying your luggage; it was a big help using giving and receiving 〜ていただく

examples.jp: 資料をチェックしていただきたいです。
examples.romaji: Shiryou o chekku shite itadakitai desu.
examples.en: I would like you to kindly check the documents.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to take a look at the materials using giving and receiving 〜ていただく

examples.jp: 先生にアドバイスをしていただきました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni adobaisu o shite itadakimashita.
examples.en: The teacher kindly gave me advice.
examples.promptEn: State that you received advice from your teacher using giving and receiving 〜ていただく

title: Verb て いただけませんか (Verb te itadakemasen ka)
short_explanation: A polite request; 'Could you please...', 'Would you mind...'
long_explanation: The て いただけませんか grammar point is used to make a polite request to someone. It is a more polite form of て くれませんか, and can be translated as 'Could you please...' or 'Would you mind...' in English. To use it, change the verb to its て-form and add いただけませんか.
formation: Verb-て form + いただけませんか

examples.jp: この手紙を投函していただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Kono tegami wo toukan shite itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please mail this letter for me?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you please mail this letter for you? using polite request 〜ていただけませんか

examples.jp: この荷物を持っていただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Kono nimotsu wo motte itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please carry this luggage for me?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you please carry this bag for you? using polite request 〜ていただけませんか

examples.jp: 隣の部屋にいる人に静かにしていただけませんか。

examples.en: Could you please ask the person next door to be quiet?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you please ask the person in the next room to be quiet? using polite request 〜ていただけませんか

examples.jp: 説明書を読んでいただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Setsumeisho wo yonde itadakemasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please read the instruction manual?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you please read the instructions? using polite request 〜ていただけませんか

title: Verb て いる (Verb-te iru)
short_explanation: Expresses an ongoing action or a state resulting from a past action.
long_explanation: The ている form is used to express either an ongoing action or a state resulting from a past action. It is formed by conjugating the verb into its て-form and then adding いる. In English, this can be translated as verb-ing or 'have verb-ed'. Its usage depends on the type of verb: action verbs or state verbs.

examples.jp: 今、本を読んでいます。
examples.romaji: Ima, hon wo yonde imasu.
examples.en: I am reading a book now.
examples.promptEn: State that you are reading a book right now using 〜ている

examples.jp: 彼は英語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo wo benkyou shite imasu.
examples.en: He is studying English.
examples.promptEn: State that he is studying English using 〜ている

examples.jp: ケーキが冷蔵庫に入っています。
examples.romaji: Keeki ga reizouko ni haitte imasu.
examples.en: The cake is in the refrigerator.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a cake in the refrigerator using 〜ている

examples.jp: 部屋がきれいになっています。
examples.romaji: Heya ga kirei ni natte imasu.
examples.en: The room has become clean.
examples.promptEn: State that the room is getting cleaner using 〜ている

title: Verb て いる ところ (Verb te iru tokoro)
short_explanation: Describes an action that is currently happening; 'in the middle of', 'in the process of'.
long_explanation: The て いる ところ grammar point is used to express an action that is currently happening or taking place. It can be translated as 'in the middle of' or 'in the process of' in English. It is formed by using the て-form of a verb followed by いる and ところ.
formation: Verb-て form + いる ところ

examples.jp: 彼は宿題をしているところです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shukudai wo shite iru tokoro desu.
examples.en: He is in the middle of doing his homework.
examples.promptEn: State that he is doing his homework right now using 〜ているところ

examples.jp: 私たちは映画を見ているところでした。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa eiga wo mite iru tokoro deshita.
examples.en: We were in the process of watching a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that we were watching a movie using 〜ているところ

examples.jp: 子供たちは公園で遊んでいるところです。
examples.romaji: Kodomotachi wa kouen de asonde iru tokoro desu.
examples.en: The kids are in the middle of playing in the park.
examples.promptEn: State that the children are playing in the park using 〜ているところ

examples.jp: 彼女はケーキを作っているところで、すぐ来ます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa keeki wo tsukutte iru tokoro de, sugu kimasu.
examples.en: She is in the process of making a cake and will come soon.
examples.promptEn: State that she's in the middle of baking a cake and will be here soon using 〜ているところ

title: Verb ている間に (te iru aida ni)
short_explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'during the time' something is happening.
long_explanation: The ～ている間に grammar point is used to express that an action or event occurs during the time another action or event is happening. It is often translated to 'while' or 'during the time' in English. It is formed by combining the て-form of a verb with いる and adding 間に.
formation: Verb-て form + いる + 間に

examples.jp: 映画を見ている間に、彼は寝てしまった。
examples.romaji: Eiga o mite iru aida ni, kare wa nete shimatta.
examples.en: While watching the movie, he fell asleep.
examples.promptEn: State that he fell asleep while watching the movie using simultaneous action 〜ている間に

examples.jp: 子供が遊んでいる間に、私は料理を作ります。
examples.romaji: Kodomo ga asonde iru aida ni, watashi wa ryouri o tsukurimasu.
examples.en: While the children are playing, I'll cook.
examples.promptEn: State that while the children are playing, you will cook using simultaneous action 〜ている間に

examples.jp: 会議が行われている間に、雨が降り始めた。
examples.romaji: Kaigi ga okonawarete iru aida ni, ame ga furihajimeta.
examples.en: While the meeting was being held, it started raining.
examples.promptEn: State that it started raining while the meeting was in progress using simultaneous action 〜ている間に

examples.jp: 彼が仕事をしている間に、私たちは買い物に行く。
examples.romaji: Kare ga shigoto o shite iru aida ni, watashitachi wa kaimono ni iku.
examples.en: While he is working, we'll go shopping.
examples.promptEn: State that while he's at work, you are going shopping using simultaneous action 〜ている間に

title: Verb ておく (〜te oku)
short_explanation: Perform an action in preparation for a future situation; 'to do something in advance'.
long_explanation: The ～ておく grammar point is used when you want to express performing an action in preparation for a future situation or to do something in advance. It is attached to the te-form of a verb and expresses the idea of doing something beforehand, as a preparatory action.

examples.jp: 駅で切符を買っておこう。
examples.romaji: Eki de kippu wo katte okou.
examples.en: Let's buy the tickets in advance at the station.
examples.promptEn: State that you will buy a ticket at the station using 〜ておく

examples.jp: 明日早く起きるために、今晩早く寝ておきます。
examples.romaji: Ashita hayaku okiru tame ni, konban hayaku nete okimasu.
examples.en: I will go to bed early tonight to wake up early tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to go to bed early tonight so you can wake up early tomorrow using 〜ておく

examples.jp: 試験前に勉強しておかないと、失敗するかもしれない。
examples.romaji: Shiken mae ni benkyou shite okanai to, shippai suru kamo shirenai.
examples.en: If I don't study in advance before the exam, I might fail.
examples.promptEn: State that if you don't study before the exam, you might fail using 〜ておく

examples.jp: 彼が到着する前に、部屋をきれいに掃除しておきましょう。
examples.romaji: Kare ga touchaku suru mae ni, heya wo kirei ni souji shite okimashou.
examples.en: Let's clean the room before he arrives.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you clean the room thoroughly before he arrives using 〜ておく

title: Verb て くださいませんか (Verb-te kudasaimasen ka)
short_explanation: Polite request for asking someone for a favor.
long_explanation: The て くださいませんか grammar point is a polite way of asking someone for a favor or requesting them to do something. It is more formal than the simple て form followed by ください, and it is commonly used in more formal settings or when speaking to someone who is not close.
formation: Verb in て-form + くださいませんか

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んでくださいませんか。
examples.romaji: Koohii o nonde kudasaimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you please drink some coffee?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to would you like some coffee? using polite request 〜てくださいませんか

examples.jp: ドアを閉めてくださいませんか。
examples.romaji: Doa o shimete kudasaimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you please close the door?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to would you mind closing the door? using polite request 〜てくださいませんか

examples.jp: 明日お昼に会ってくださいませんか。
examples.romaji: Ashita ohiru ni atte kudasaimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you please meet me at lunch tomorrow?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to would you mind meeting you tomorrow at lunchtime? using polite request 〜てくださいませんか

examples.jp: その資料を送ってくださいませんか。
examples.romaji: Sono shiryou o okutte kudasaimasen ka.
examples.en: Would you please send me that document?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you please send you that document? using polite request 〜てくださいませんか

title: Verb て くださる (Verb-te kudasaru)
short_explanation: Expresses gratitude for receiving someone's favor; 'to kindly do'.
long_explanation: The て くださる grammar point is used to express gratitude for receiving a favor or action from someone else. It is an honorific way to say that someone kindly does something for the speaker or the listener. The verb is conjugated to its ～て form and followed by くださる.

examples.jp: 先生が手伝ってくださる。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga tetsudatte kudasaru.
examples.en: The teacher kindly helps.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher will help you using giving and receiving 〜てくださる

examples.jp: お母さんが美味しい料理を作ってくださる。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ga oishii ryouri wo tsukutte kudasaru.
examples.en: My mother kindly cooks delicious meals.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom makes delicious meals for you using giving and receiving 〜てくださる

examples.jp: 友達が私を駅まで送ってくださる。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi wo eki made okutte kudasaru.
examples.en: My friend kindly gives me a ride to the station.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend is taking you to the station using giving and receiving 〜てくださる

examples.jp: 部長がすぐに質問に答えてくださる。
examples.romaji: Buchou ga sugu ni shitsumon ni kotaete kudasaru.
examples.en: The manager kindly answers the questions immediately.
examples.promptEn: State that the department head answers your questions right away using giving and receiving 〜てくださる

title: Verb て くる (Verb te kuru)
short_explanation: An action that starts in the past and continues to the present or future; 'come to', 'begin to', 'become'.
long_explanation: The て くる grammar point is used to express an action that starts in the past and continues to the present or future. It can also show a change in state or condition. The formation involves attaching the て-form of the verb followed by くる.

examples.jp: 最近、日本語が分かってくるようになりました。
examples.romaji: Saikin, nihongo ga wakatte kuru you ni narimashita.
examples.en: Recently, I've come to understand Japanese.
examples.promptEn: State that lately, you have started to understand Japanese better using change of state 〜てくる

examples.jp: 寒くなってきたので、コートを着ましょう。
examples.romaji: Samuku natte kita node, kooto wo kimashou.
examples.en: Since it's gotten cold, let's put on a coat.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you it's getting cold, so let's put on your coats using change of state 〜てくる

examples.jp: 雨がやんできました。
examples.romaji: Ame ga yande kimashita.
examples.en: The rain has stopped (and it's cleared up).
examples.promptEn: State that the rain has let up using change of state 〜てくる

examples.jp: 彼がだんだん怖くなってきた。
examples.romaji: Kare ga dandan kowaku natte kita.
examples.en: He has become progressively scarier.
examples.promptEn: State that you are starting to get scared of him using change of state 〜てくる

title: Verb てくれませんか (〜te kuremasen ka)
short_explanation: A polite way to request someone to do something for you; 'Could you please', 'Would you please', 'Won't you'.
long_explanation: The ～てくれませんか grammar point is used to ask someone politely to do something for you. It is formed by using the て-form of a verb followed by くれませんか. It translates to 'Could you please', 'Would you please', or 'Won't you' in English.
formation: Verb-て form + くれませんか

examples.jp: ドアを開けてくれませんか。
examples.romaji: Doa wo akete kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please open the door?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you open the door for you? using request 〜てくれませんか

examples.jp: これを見てくれませんか。
examples.romaji: Kore wo mite kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Would you please take a look at this?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you take a look at this? using request 〜てくれませんか

examples.jp: 手伝ってくれませんか。
examples.romaji: Tetsudatte kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Won't you help me?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you help you? using request 〜てくれませんか

examples.jp: 明日、迎えに来てくれませんか。
examples.romaji: Ashita, mukae ni kite kuremasen ka.
examples.en: Could you please come to pick me up tomorrow?
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to could you come pick you up tomorrow? using request 〜てくれませんか

title: Verb て くれる (Verb-te kureru)
short_explanation: Expresses that someone does something for the speaker (or another person in speaker's group); 'to do something for me/us'.
long_explanation: The て くれる grammar point is used to express when someone does something for, or gives something to the speaker (or someone in the speaker's group). The action is usually done willingly or as a favor by the person performing the action. It is usually translated into English as 'to do something for me' or 'to give something to me'.

examples.jp: 友達が宿題を手伝ってくれました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga shukudai wo tetsudatte kuremashita.
examples.en: My friend helped me with my homework.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to my friend helped you with your homework using request 〜てくれる

examples.jp: 弟が部屋を掃除してくれた。
examples.romaji: Otouto ga heya wo souji shite kureta.
examples.en: My younger brother cleaned the room for me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to my younger brother cleaned your room for you using request 〜てくれる

examples.jp: 先生が質問に答えてくれます。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga shitsumon ni kotaete kuremasu.
examples.en: The teacher answers my questions for me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to the teacher will answer your questions using request 〜てくれる

examples.jp: 彼女が手紙を書いてくれる。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga tegami wo kaite kureru.
examples.en: She writes a letter for me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to she writes you a letter using request 〜てくれる

title: Verb て + さしあげる (Verb TE sashiageru)
short_explanation: A polite way to express giving or doing something for someone.
long_explanation: The grammar point 'Verb て + さしあげる' is used to express the action of giving or doing something for someone in a polite manner. It is mainly used when the speaker is offering or doing something for someone of higher social status or showing respect towards the person. To form this expression, you need to conjugate the verb into its て-form and attach さしあげる.

examples.jp: お茶を入れてさしあげます。
examples.romaji: Ocha wo irete sashiagemasu.
examples.en: I will prepare and serve tea (for you).
examples.promptEn: State that you will make you some tea using giving and receiving 〜て+さしあげる

examples.jp: メッセージを送ってさしあげました。
examples.romaji: Messeiji wo okutte sashiagemashita.
examples.en: I have sent the message (for you).
examples.promptEn: State that you sent you a message using giving and receiving 〜て+さしあげる

examples.jp: 荷物を持ってさしあげましょうか。
examples.romaji: Nimotsu wo motte sashiagemashou ka.
examples.en: Shall I carry the luggage (for you)?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you would you like you to carry your luggage for you? using giving and receiving 〜て+さしあげる

examples.jp: お電話をかけてさしあげます。
examples.romaji: Odenwa wo kakete sashiagemasu.
examples.en: I will make a phone call (for you).
examples.promptEn: State that you will give you a call using giving and receiving 〜て+さしあげる

title: Verb てしまう (〜te shimau)
short_explanation: Expresses unintentional actions or actions with regrettable outcomes; 'to end up doing', 'to accidentally do'.
long_explanation: The ～てしまう grammar point is used to indicate unintentional actions or actions with regrettable outcomes. It can often be translated as 'to end up doing' or 'to accidentally do' in English. The formation requires adding しまう to the て-form of a verb.

examples.jp: ケーキを全部食べてしまった。
examples.romaji: Keeki wo zenbu tabete shimatta.
examples.en: I ended up eating the whole cake.
examples.promptEn: State that you ate the whole cake using intention 〜てしまう

examples.jp: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo wasurete shimaimashita.
examples.en: I accidentally forgot my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you forgot your homework using intention 〜てしまう

examples.jp: 彼に秘密を言ってしまった。
examples.romaji: Kare ni himitsu wo itte shimatta.
examples.en: I accidentally told him the secret.
examples.promptEn: State that you let him in on the secret using intention 〜てしまう

examples.jp: 値札を見ずに高い服を買ってしまった。
examples.romaji: Nefuda wo mizu ni takai fuku wo katte shimatta.
examples.en: I ended up buying expensive clothes without looking at the price tag.
examples.promptEn: State that you ended up buying an expensive piece of clothing without checking the price tag using intention 〜てしまう

title: Verb て ほしい (Verb-te hoshii)
short_explanation: Express a desire for someone else to do something; 'I want (someone) to'.
long_explanation: The て ほしい grammar point is used to express the speaker's desire for someone else to do an action. It is formed by combining the て-form of a verb with ほしい. The subject is usually followed by the particle に, but it can be dropped in casual speech.

examples.jp: 子供にもっと勉強してほしい。
examples.romaji: Kodomo ni motto benkyou shite hoshii.
examples.en: I want my child to study more.
examples.promptEn: State that you want your child to study more using desire 〜てほしい

examples.jp: 彼にもっと早く来てほしい。
examples.romaji: Kare ni motto hayaku kite hoshii.
examples.en: I want him to come earlier.
examples.promptEn: State that you want him to come sooner using desire 〜てほしい

examples.jp: 友達にその本を読んでほしい。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni sono hon o yonde hoshii.
examples.en: I want my friend to read that book.
examples.promptEn: State that you want your friend to read that book using desire 〜てほしい

examples.jp: 先生に質問に答えてほしい。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni shitsumon ni kotaete hoshii.
examples.en: I want the teacher to answer the question.
examples.promptEn: State that you want the teacher to answer your question using desire 〜てほしい

title: Verb てみる (〜te miru)
short_explanation: Used to express 'try to' or 'attempt to do'.
long_explanation: The ～てみる grammar point is used with verbs to express 'trying' or 'attempting' to do something. It emphasizes the idea of giving something a go or trying it out, often to see what the results or outcome will be.

examples.jp: この料理を作ってみます。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri o tsukutte mimasu.
examples.en: I will try to make this dish.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to try making this dish using 〜てみる

examples.jp: その服を着てみてください。

examples.en: Please try on those clothes.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to try on that outfit using 〜てみる

examples.jp: 新しいレストランに行ってみよう。
examples.romaji: Atarashii resutoran ni itte miyou.
examples.en: Let's try going to the new restaurant.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you try going to a new restaurant using 〜てみる

examples.jp: 映画を見てみたいです。
examples.romaji: Eiga o mite mitai desu.
examples.en: I want to try watching the movie.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to watch a movie using 〜てみる

title: Verb てもらいたい (～te moraitai)
short_explanation: Express a desire to receive a favor or service from someone else.
long_explanation: The ～てもらいたい grammar point is used to express one's desire to receive a favor, service, or action from someone else. It is formed by attaching もらいたい to the て-form of verbs. This structure emphasizes the help or favor the speaker wants from someone else.

examples.jp: この荷物を運んでもらいたいです。
examples.romaji: Kono nimotsu o hakonde moraitai desu.
examples.en: I want you to carry this luggage for me.
examples.promptEn: State that you would like you to carry this package using desire 〜てもらいたい

examples.jp: 彼にそのニュースを教えてもらいたい。
examples.romaji: Kare ni sono nyuusu o oshiete moraitai.
examples.en: I want him to tell me the news.
examples.promptEn: State that you want him to tell you that news using desire 〜てもらいたい

examples.jp: 友達に日本語を教えてもらいたい。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni Nihongo o oshiete moraitai.

examples.promptEn: State that you want your friend to teach you Japanese using desire 〜てもらいたい

examples.jp: スタッフにチェックインの方法を説明してもらいたい。

title: Verb て もらう (Verb-te morau)
short_explanation: Express receiving a favor or action from someone.
long_explanation: The Verb て もらう grammar point is used to express that the speaker or a third person receives a favor or action from someone else. It describes an action performed by someone for the benefit of the speaker or a third person, implying gratitude or request from the beneficiary.

examples.jp: 友達に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni shukudai o tetsudatte moratta.
examples.en: I had my friend help me with my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that a friend helped you with your homework using giving and receiving 〜てもらう

examples.jp: 母に部屋を掃除してもらいました。
examples.romaji: Haha ni heya o souji shite moraimashita.
examples.en: I had my mother clean my room.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom cleaned your room for you using giving and receiving 〜てもらう

examples.jp: 彼に荷物を持ってもらいたい。
examples.romaji: Kare ni nimotsu o motte moraitai.
examples.en: I want him to carry my luggage for me.
examples.promptEn: State that you want him to carry your luggage using giving and receiving 〜てもらう

examples.jp: 先生に質問に答えてもらえますか？
examples.romaji: Sensei ni shitsumon ni kotaete moraemasu ka?
examples.en: Can I have the teacher answer my question?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether could you please answer your question, teacher using giving and receiving 〜てもらう

title: Verb てもらえませんか (～te moraemasen ka)
short_explanation: A polite way to ask for a favor or request someone to do something.
long_explanation: The ～てもらえませんか grammar point is a polite and indirect way of asking someone to do something for you or asking for a favor. It is formed by conjugating the verb into the て-form and adding もらえませんか. This form is used in conversations to show politeness and humility.
formation: Verb-て form + もらえませんか

examples.jp: この手紙を見てもらえませんか。
examples.romaji: Kono tegami o mite moraemasen ka?
examples.en: Could you take a look at this letter for me?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you could you please take a look at this letter? using request 〜てもらえませんか

examples.jp: 荷物を持ってもらえませんか。
examples.romaji: Nimotsu o motte moraemasen ka?
examples.en: Could you carry this luggage for me?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you could you please carry your luggage for you? using request 〜てもらえませんか

examples.jp: 部屋を掃除してもらえませんか。
examples.romaji: Heya o souji shite moraemasen ka?
examples.en: Could you clean the room for me?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you could you please clean the room? using request 〜てもらえませんか

examples.jp: 明日のミーティングに参加してもらえませんか。
examples.romaji: Ashita no miitingu ni sanka shite moraemasen ka?
examples.en: Could you attend tomorrow's meeting for me?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you could you please attend tomorrow's meeting? using request 〜てもらえませんか

title: Verb ない ことがある (Verb-nai koto ga aru)
short_explanation: Expresses that something doesn't always happen or there are occasions when it doesn't happen.
long_explanation: The ないことがある grammar point is used to indicate that there are instances or times when something doesn't happen or isn't done. It is formed by combining the negative form of a verb (ない) with ことがある.

examples.jp: 彼は会議に出席しないことがある。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kaigi ni shusseki shinai koto ga aru.
examples.en: There are times when he doesn't attend meetings.
examples.promptEn: State that he sometimes does not attend meetings using experience 〜ないことがある

examples.jp: この電車は定刻に来ないことがある。
examples.romaji: Kono densha wa teikoku ni konai koto ga aru.
examples.en: There are occasions when this train doesn't come on time.
examples.promptEn: State that this train sometimes doesn't arrive on time using experience 〜ないことがある

examples.jp: 私は朝食を食べないことがある。
