title: Verb るときに (〜ru toki ni)
short_explanation: Describes the time when a certain action takes place; 'when', 'at the time'.
long_explanation: The ～るときに grammar point is used to indicate the time when a certain action or event happens. It can be translated as 'when' or 'at the time' in English. The formation involves attaching ときに to the verb in its dictionary (る) form.

examples.jp: 映画を見るときに、ポップコーンを食べます。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo miru toki ni, poppukoon wo tabemasu.
examples.en: When I watch a movie, I eat popcorn.
examples.promptEn: State that you eat popcorn when you watch movies using desire 〜るときに

examples.jp: 寝るときに、部屋の電気を消します。
examples.romaji: Neru toki ni, heya no denki wo keshimasu.
examples.en: When I go to bed, I turn off the room lights.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you go to bed, you turn off the lights in your room using desire 〜るときに

examples.jp: 運動するときに、水分補給が大切です。
examples.romaji: Undou suru toki ni, suibun hokyuu ga taisetsu desu.
examples.en: When exercising, it's important to stay hydrated.
examples.promptEn: State that it's important to stay hydrated when exercising using desire 〜るときに

examples.jp: 旅行するときに、カメラを持っていくことが好きです。
examples.romaji: Ryokou suru toki ni, kamera wo motteiku koto ga suki desu.
examples.en: When I travel, I like to bring a camera.
examples.promptEn: State that you like to bring your camera with you when you travel using desire 〜るときに

title: Verb る ところ (Verb-ru tokoro)
short_explanation: Expresses the state or moment when an action is about to happen or is happening.
long_explanation: The grammar point 'Verb る ところ' is used to express that one is just about to do something, or is in the process of doing it. It can be translated as 'just about to' or 'in the middle of' in English, depending on context.

examples.jp: 彼は食べるところです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa taberu tokoro desu.
examples.en: He is in the process of eating.
examples.promptEn: State that he is eating using 〜るところ

examples.jp: 私は出かけるところです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa dekakeru tokoro desu.
examples.en: I am just about to leave.
examples.promptEn: State that you are about to go out using 〜るところ

examples.jp: 彼女は泣くところでした。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa naku tokoro deshita.
examples.en: She was on the verge of crying.
examples.promptEn: State that she was about to cry using 〜るところ

examples.jp: 私たちは勉強するところです。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa benkyou suru tokoro desu.
examples.en: We are in the middle of studying.
examples.promptEn: State that this is where you study using 〜るところ

title: Verb 出す (~dasu)
short_explanation: Express the action of taking something out, starting an action, or emphasizing a verb.
long_explanation: The verb 出す (~dasu) is used to express the action of taking something out, starting an action, or emphasizing the verb it is attached to. To form this grammar point, simply attach 出す (~dasu) to the stem of the verb.

examples.jp: 本を棚から出してください。
examples.romaji: Hon o tana kara dashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please take the book out from the shelf.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to take the book off the shelf using 〜出す

examples.jp: 彼は部屋から急いで出ました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa heya kara isoide demashita.
examples.en: He rushed out of the room.
examples.promptEn: State that he hurried out of the room using 〜出す

examples.jp: 授業が始まる前に宿題を出してください。
examples.romaji: Jugyou ga hajimaru mae ni shukudai wo dashite kudasai.
examples.en: Submit your homework before class starts.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to assign the homework before class begins using 〜出す

examples.jp: 彼女は歌い出しました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa utaidashimashita.
examples.en: She began to sing.
examples.promptEn: State that she started singing using 〜出す

title: Verb 方 (〜hou)
short_explanation: Indicates the way or method of doing something; often read as '～かた' ('how to', 'the way of').
long_explanation: The ～方 grammar point is used to express the way or method of doing something, similar to 'how to' or 'the way of' in English. It can be attached to the stem of a verb to form a noun that indicates the method of doing the action. In practice, ～方 is usually read as '～かた' (e.g., 作り方＝つくりかた).

examples.jp: 誰かがケーキの作り方を知っていますか？
examples.romaji: Dareka ga keeki no tsukurikata o shitteimasu ka?
examples.en: Does anyone know how to make a cake?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether does anyone know how to make a cake using 〜方

examples.jp: 彼女は英語の話し方を学んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo no hanashikata o manandeimasu.
examples.en: She is learning how to speak English.
examples.promptEn: State that she is learning how to speak English using 〜方

examples.jp: このパソコンの使い方を教えてください。
examples.romaji: Kono pasokon no tsukaikata o oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Please teach me how to use this computer.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to teach you how to use this computer using 〜方

examples.jp: 数学の問題の解き方を覚えるのが難しいです。
examples.romaji: Suugaku no mondai no tokikata o oboeru no ga muzukashii desu.
examples.en: It is difficult to remember the way to solve math problems.
examples.promptEn: State that it's hard to learn how to solve math problems using 〜方

title: Verb 終わる (〜owaru)
short_explanation: Verbal action is completed; 'to finish', 'to end'.
long_explanation: The verb 終わる (owaru) is used to express that an action has been completed or something has come to an end. Despite ending in る, 終わる is a godan (u-verb), so it does not follow the typical ichidan (る-verb) conjugation. It is translated as 'to finish', 'to end' or 'to be over' in English.

examples.jp: 映画が終わったら、家に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Eiga ga owattara, ie ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: When the movie finishes, I'll go home.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when the movie is over, you will go home using 〜終わる

examples.jp: 仕事が終わるまで、待ってください。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owaru made, matte kudasai.
examples.en: Please wait until the work is finished.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to wait until you finish work using 〜終わる

examples.jp: パーティーはもうすぐ終わります。
examples.romaji: Paatii wa mou sugu owarimasu.
examples.en: The party will be over soon.
examples.promptEn: State that the party is about to end using 〜終わる

examples.jp: 試験が終わったら、友達と遊びに行く予定です。
examples.romaji: Shiken ga owattara, tomodachi to asobi ni iku yotei desu.
examples.en: Once the exam is over, I plan to go out with my friends.
examples.promptEn: State that after the exam, you plan to go out with your friends using 〜終わる

title: Verb + 続ける (つづける, tsuzukeru)
short_explanation: To continue doing or to keep doing an action.
long_explanation: The grammar point 続ける (tsuzukeru) is attached to the masu-stem form of verbs, and it indicates the ongoing continuity of an action. It can be translated as 'to continue doing' or 'to keep doing' in English.

examples.jp: 彼は毎日ジムで運動を続けています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mainichi jimu de undou o tsuzuketeimasu.
examples.en: He continues to exercise at the gym every day.
examples.promptEn: State that he continues to work out at the gym every day using 〜続ける

examples.jp: 彼女は勉強を続けるために図書館に行きました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa benkyou o tsuzukeru tame ni toshokan ni ikimashita.
examples.en: She went to the library to continue studying.
examples.promptEn: State that she went to the library to continue studying using 〜続ける

examples.jp: 私たちは雨にも関わらず散歩を続けました。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa ame ni mo kakawarazu sanpo o tsuzukemashita.
examples.en: We continued walking despite the rain.
examples.promptEn: State that we continued your walk despite the rain using 〜続ける

examples.jp: 彼は仕事を続けることに決めた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shigoto o tsuzukeru koto ni kimeta.
examples.en: He decided to continue working.
examples.promptEn: State that he decided to continue working using 〜続ける

title: ～かしら (〜kashira)
short_explanation: Indicates uncertainty or doubt; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
long_explanation: The ～かしら grammar point is used to express uncertainty or doubt about a situation. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'I'm not sure' in English. It is primarily used by females in casual conversations but can be used by males in some contexts as well. ～かしら is used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Verb-casual + かしら, い-Adjective + かしら, な-Adjective + かしら, Noun + かしら

examples.jp: 今日は雨が降るかしら？
examples.romaji: Kyou wa ame ga furu kashira?
examples.en: I wonder if it will rain today?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether you wonder if it will rain today using desire 〜かしら

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しいかしら？
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii kashira?
examples.en: I wonder if this cake is delicious?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether you wonder if this cake is delicious using desire 〜かしら

examples.jp: 彼は病気かしら？
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki kashira?
examples.en: I wonder if he is sick?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether you wonder if he's sick using desire 〜かしら

examples.jp: 彼女は学生かしら？
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei kashira?
examples.en: I wonder if she is a student?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether you wonder if she's a student using desire 〜かしら

title: ～かどうか (〜ka dou ka)
short_explanation: Used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements.
long_explanation: The ～かどうか grammar point is used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements. It is often used to express uncertainty or to inquire about information in a more polite form. ～かどうか can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Verb-casual + かどうか, い-Adjective + かどうか, な-Adjective + (だ)かどうか, Noun + (だ)かどうか

examples.jp: 彼が来るかどうか知りません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga kuru ka dou ka shirimasen.
examples.en: I don't know if he will come or not.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't know if he's coming using 〜かどうか

examples.jp: この本が面白いかどうか教えてください。
examples.romaji: Kono hon ga omoshiroi ka dou ka oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Please tell me if this book is interesting or not.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to let you know if you find this book interesting using 〜かどうか

examples.jp: 彼女が綺麗だかどうかは分かりません。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga kirei da ka dou ka wa wakarimasen.
examples.en: I don't know whether she is beautiful or not.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't know if she's pretty using 〜かどうか

examples.jp: 彼が先生だかどうか覚えていません。
examples.romaji: Kare ga sensei da ka dou ka oboete imasen.
examples.en: I don't remember if he is a teacher or not.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't remember if he's a teacher using 〜かどうか

title: ～かなあ (〜kanaa)
short_explanation: Expresses uncertainty or wonder; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
long_explanation: The ～かなあ grammar point is used to express a feeling of uncertainty or wonder about a situation or statement. It can be translated as 'I wonder' or 'I'm not sure' in English. In casual spoken Japanese, when using nouns or な-adjectives before かなあ, the copula だ is often omitted or replaced with の (e.g., 学生かなあ or 学生なのかなあ). This grammar point should not be used when asking questions directly to someone, as it may come off as too direct or impolite.
formation: Verb-casual + かなあ, い-Adjective + かなあ, (な-Adjective/Noun) + (だ) + かなあ

examples.jp: 明日雨が降るかなあ。
examples.romaji: Ashita ame ga furu kanaa.
examples.en: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you wonder if it will rain tomorrow using desire 〜かなあ

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しいかなあ。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii kanaa.
examples.en: I wonder if this cake is delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that you wonder if this cake is delicious using desire 〜かなあ

examples.jp: 彼は病気かなあ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki kanaa.
examples.en: I wonder if he is sick.
examples.promptEn: State that you wonder if he's sick using desire 〜かなあ

examples.jp: 彼女は学生かなあ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei kanaa.
examples.en: I wonder if she is a student.
examples.promptEn: State that you wonder if she's a student using desire 〜かなあ

title: ～かもしれない (〜kamoshirenai)
short_explanation: Express uncertainty; 'maybe', 'might', 'possibly'.
long_explanation: The ～かもしれない grammar point is used to express uncertainty or the possibility of something occurring. It can be translated as 'maybe', 'might', or 'possibly' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun. In everyday speech, speakers often omit だ before かもしれない for nouns and な-adjectives.
formation: Verb-casual + かもしれない, い-Adjective + かもしれない, な-Adjective + だかもしれない, Noun + だかもしれない

examples.jp: 明日雨が降るかもしれない。
examples.romaji: Ashita ame ga furu kamoshirenai.
examples.en: It might rain tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that it might rain tomorrow using desire 〜かもしれない

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しいかもしれない。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii kamoshirenai.
examples.en: This cake might be delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this cake might be delicious using desire 〜かもしれない

examples.jp: 彼が病気かもしれない。
examples.romaji: Kare ga byouki kamoshirenai.
examples.en: He might be sick.
examples.promptEn: State that he might be sick using desire 〜かもしれない

examples.jp: 彼女は学生かもしれない。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei kamoshirenai.
examples.en: She might be a student.
examples.promptEn: State that she might be a student using desire 〜かもしれない

title: ～から (〜kara)
short_explanation: Express a reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
long_explanation: The ～から grammar point is used to express a reason, cause, or the origin of something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + から, い-Adjective + から, な-Adjective + だから, Noun + だから

examples.jp: 雨が降るから、傘を持って行ってください。
examples.romaji: Ame ga furu kara, kasa wo motte itte kudasai.
examples.en: Because it's raining, please bring an umbrella.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to it's going to rain, so please take an umbrella with you using reason 〜から

examples.jp: このケーキは美味しいから、みんな食べるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii kara, minna taberu deshou.
examples.en: Because this cake is delicious, everyone will probably eat it.
examples.promptEn: State that this cake is delicious, so you are sure everyone will eat it using reason 〜から

examples.jp: 彼は病気だから、学校を休みます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki dakara, gakkou wo yasumimasu.
examples.en: He will be absent from school because he is sick.
examples.promptEn: State that he is sick, so he will be absent from school using reason 〜から

examples.jp: 今日は日曜日だから、学校がありません。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa nichiyoubi dakara, gakkou ga arimasen.
examples.en: There is no school today because it is Sunday.
examples.promptEn: State that today is Sunday, so there is no school using reason 〜から

title: ～けれど (〜keredo)
short_explanation: Indicate a soft contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however'.
long_explanation: The ～けれど grammar point is used to express a soft contrast or contradiction between two statements. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however' in English. It is relatively informal and can be replaced by more formal expressions like けれども or が. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + けれど, い-Adjective + けれど, な-Adjective + だけれど, Noun + だけれど

examples.jp: 今日は忙しいけれど、明日はもっと時間がある。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa isogashii keredo, ashita wa motto jikan ga aru.
examples.en: I'm busy today, but I have more time tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you are busy today, but you will have more time tomorrow using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: このレストランは高いけれど、料理が美味しい。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran wa takai keredo, ryouri ga oishii.
examples.en: This restaurant is expensive, but the food is delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant is expensive, but the food is delicious using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: 彼は若いけれど、とても経験豊富だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa wakai keredo, totemo keiken houfu da.
examples.en: He is young, but he is very experienced.
examples.promptEn: State that he is young, but very experienced using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: 彼女は病気だけれど、明るく元気だ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa byouki da keredo, akaruku genki da.
examples.en: She is sick, but she is cheerful and energetic.
examples.promptEn: State that she is sick, but she is cheerful and full of energy using contrast 〜けれど

title: ～させてください (〜sasete kudasai)
short_explanation: Express a polite request to allow or permit someone to do something.
long_explanation: The ～させてください grammar point is used to make a polite request to allow or permit someone to do something. It can be translated as 'please let me' or 'please allow me to' in English. It is formed by taking the causative form of a verb and adding ください.

examples.jp: もう少し考えさせてください。
examples.romaji: Mou sukoshi kangaesasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me think a little more.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to give you a little more time to think about this using polite request 〜させてください

examples.jp: 写真を撮らせてください。
examples.romaji: Shashin o torasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me take a photo.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to let you take a photo using polite request 〜させてください

examples.jp: もうちょっと練習させてください。
examples.romaji: Mou chotto renshuu sasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me practice a little more.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to let you practice a little more using polite request 〜させてください

examples.jp: ここで待たせてください。
examples.romaji: Koko de matasete kudasai.
examples.en: Please let me wait here.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to hold on a moment using polite request 〜させてください

title: ～し、～し、～ (〜shi, 〜shi, 〜)
short_explanation: Express multiple reasons or characteristics; 'and', 'because', 'since'.
long_explanation: The ～し、～し、～ grammar point is used to connect multiple reasons or characteristics that support a conclusion or statement. It can be translated as 'and', 'because', or 'since' in English. This grammar can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Verb-casual + し, い-Adjective + し, な-Adjective + だし, Noun + だし

examples.jp: 彼は若いし、元気だし、フレンドリーだし、みんなと仲良くなれると思います。
examples.romaji: Kare wa wakai shi, genki da shi, furendorī da shi, minna to nakayoku nareru to omoimasu.
examples.en: He is young, energetic, friendly, and I think he can get along with everyone.
examples.promptEn: State that he's young, energetic, and friendly, so you think he'll get along well with everyone using reason 〜し～し

examples.jp: このレストランは料理が美味しいし、雰囲気がいいし、価格も手頃だからお勧めです。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran wa ryouri ga oishii shi, fun'iki ga ii shi, kakaku mo tegoro dakara osusume desu.
examples.en: I recommend this restaurant because the food is delicious, the atmosphere is nice, and the prices are reasonable.
examples.promptEn: State that you recommend this restaurant because the food is delicious, the atmosphere is great, and the prices are reasonable using reason 〜し～し

examples.jp: 彼女は勉強ができるし、スポーツも得意だし、性格もいい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa benkyou ga dekiru shi, supōtsu mo tokui da shi, seikaku mo ii.
examples.en: She is good at studying, good at sports, and has a good personality.
examples.promptEn: State that she is good at her studies, good at sports, and has a great personality using reason 〜し～し

examples.jp: 今日は寒いし、雨も降っているし、家でゆっくり休んだ方がいいでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa samui shi, ame mo futte iru shi, ie de yukkuri yasunda hou ga ii deshou.
examples.en: It's cold today, and it's raining, so it's better to relax at home.
examples.promptEn: State that it's cold today, and it's raining, so you should probably just relax at home using reason 〜し～し

title: ～すぎる (〜sugiru)
short_explanation: Expresses that something is excessive or overdone; 'too much', 'too', 'over'.
long_explanation: The ～すぎる grammar point is used to express that something is excessive or beyond a certain level. It can be translated as 'too much', 'too', or 'over' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, or な-adjective.
formation: Verb-stem + すぎる, い-Adjective (remove い) + すぎる, な-Adjective + すぎる

examples.jp: この部屋は暑すぎる。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa atsui sugiru.
examples.en: This room is too hot.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is too hot using excess 〜すぎる

examples.jp: 彼は早く来すぎた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa hayaku kisugita.
examples.en: He came too early.
examples.promptEn: State that he arrived too early using excess 〜すぎる

examples.jp: この箱は重すぎて持ち上げられない。
examples.romaji: Kono hako wa omosugite mochiagerarenai.
examples.en: This box is too heavy to lift.
examples.promptEn: State that this box is too heavy to lift using excess 〜すぎる

examples.jp: 彼女は忙しくて遊びすぎはしない。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa isogashikute asobisugi wa shinai.
examples.en: She's too busy to play too much.
examples.promptEn: State that she's too busy to go out too much using excess 〜すぎる

title: ～ずつ (〜zutsu)
short_explanation: Indicates equal distribution; 'each', 'per', 'apiece'.
long_explanation: The ～ずつ grammar point is used to express an equal distribution of something, whether it is an action, an amount, or an item. It is translated as 'each', 'per', or 'apiece' in English.

examples.jp: りんごを2つずつ配ります。
examples.romaji: Ringo wo futatsu zutsu kubarimasu.
examples.en: I will distribute 2 apples each.
examples.promptEn: State that you will hand out two apples to each person using contrast 〜ずつ

examples.jp: 私たちは週に一度ずつ掃除をします。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa shuu ni ichido zutsu souji o shimasu.
examples.en: We each clean once per week.
examples.promptEn: State that we clean once a week using contrast 〜ずつ

examples.jp: みんなは同じ距離を一歩ずつ歩いた。
examples.romaji: Minna wa onaji kyori o ippo zutsu aruita.
examples.en: Everyone walked the same distance, one step at a time.
examples.promptEn: State that everyone walked the same distance, one step at a time using contrast 〜ずつ

examples.jp: 彼女は子供たちに一枚ずつプレゼントをくれました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kodomotachi ni ichimai zutsu purezento o kuremashita.
examples.en: She gave one present to each child.
examples.promptEn: State that she gave the children one present each using contrast 〜ずつ

title: ～そうだ (〜sou da)

short_explanation: Express one's thoughts or opinions; 'I think', 'I believe'.
long_explanation: The ～と思う grammar point is used to express one's thoughts or opinions on a particular subject or situation. It can be translated as 'I think' or 'I believe' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + と思う, い-Adjective + と思う, な-Adjective + だと思う, Noun + だと思う

examples.jp: 明日晴れると思います。
examples.romaji: Ashita hareru to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you think it will be sunny tomorrow using 〜と思う

examples.jp: この映画は面白いと思う。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa omoshiroi to omou.
examples.en: I think this movie is interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that you think this movie is interesting using 〜と思う

examples.jp: 彼は親切だと思います。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu da to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think he is kind.
examples.promptEn: State that you think he is kind using 〜と思う

examples.jp: 鈴木さんは先生だと思う。
examples.romaji: Suzuki-san wa sensei da to omou.
examples.en: I think Suzuki-san is a teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you think Mr. Suzuki is a teacher using 〜と思う

title: ～という (〜to iu)
short_explanation: Used to quote, express hearsay or define something.
long_explanation: The ～という grammar point is used to quote someone's words, express something you heard or read from someone else, or define and clarify the subject. It can be translated as 'called', 'that', or 'it is said'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + という, い-Adjective + という, な-Adjective + という, Noun + という

examples.jp: 彼は「好きだ」と言った。
examples.romaji: Kare wa 'suki da' to itta.
examples.en: He said 'I like you'.
examples.promptEn: State that he said, "you like it." using 〜という

examples.jp: その映画は面白いという評判があります。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa omoshiroi to iu hyouban ga arimasu.
examples.en: The movie has a reputation for being interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie has a reputation for being entertaining using 〜という

examples.jp: 日本には富士山という高い山があります。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni wa Fujisan to iu takai yama ga arimasu.
examples.en: In Japan, there is a tall mountain called Mount Fuji.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a tall mountain in Japan called Mount Fuji using 〜という

examples.jp: 彼女は難しい仕事をしているという話です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa muzukashii shigoto o shiteiru to iu hanashi desu.
examples.en: I heard she is doing a difficult job.
examples.promptEn: State that the story is about her doing a difficult job using 〜という

title: ～ないといけない (〜nai to ikenai)
short_explanation: Express a necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
long_explanation: The ～ないといけない grammar point is used to express a sense of necessity or obligation, similar to 'must', 'have to', or 'need to' in English. This structure is formed by using the negative form of the verb (ending in ない) followed by といけない.

examples.jp: 明日試験があるから、今夜勉強しないといけない。
examples.romaji: Ashita shiken ga aru kara, kon'ya benkyou shinai to ikenai.
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study tonight.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a test tomorrow, so you have to study tonight using obligation 〜ないといけない

examples.jp: ９時に出発しないといけない。
examples.romaji: Ku-ji ni shuppatsu shinai to ikenai.
examples.en: We must leave at 9 o'clock.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to leave at 9:00 using obligation 〜ないといけない

examples.jp: 風邪をひかないように、手をよく洗わないといけない。
examples.romaji: Kaze o hikanai you ni, te o yoku arawanai to ikenai.
examples.en: To avoid catching a cold, we have to wash our hands well.
examples.promptEn: State that to avoid catching a cold, you have to wash your hands thoroughly using obligation 〜ないといけない

examples.jp: この仕事は明日までに終わらないといけない。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa ashita made ni owaranai to ikenai.
examples.en: This work must be finished by tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that this work has to be finished by tomorrow using obligation 〜ないといけない

title: ～なきゃいけない (〜nakya ikenai)
short_explanation: Express a necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
long_explanation: The ～なきゃいけない grammar point is used to express a sense of necessity or obligation, similar to saying 'must' or 'have to' in English. It is a casual and more colloquial form of the ～なければいけない grammar point. The formation is different for verbs, but it is not used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
formation: Verb-casual (negative form without い) + なきゃいけない

examples.jp: 明日までに宿題を終わらなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Ashita made ni shukudai wo owaranakya ikenai.
examples.en: I have to finish my homework by tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to finish your homework by tomorrow using obligation 〜なきゃいけない

examples.jp: もうすぐ出かけるから、急いで準備しなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu dekakeru kara, isoide junbi shinakya ikenai.
examples.en: We're leaving soon, so I have to hurry and get ready.
examples.promptEn: State that you are about to go out, so you have to hurry and get ready using obligation 〜なきゃいけない

examples.jp: このプロジェクトは来週提出しなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Kono purojekuto wa raishuu teishutsu shinakya ikenai.
examples.en: I must submit this project by next week.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to turn in this project next week using obligation 〜なきゃいけない

examples.jp: 電車に乗る前に、切符を買わなきゃいけない。
examples.romaji: Densha ni noru mae ni, kippu wo kawanakya ikenai.
examples.en: I have to buy a ticket before getting on the train.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to buy a ticket before getting on the train using obligation 〜なきゃいけない

title: ～なくちゃいけない (〜naku cha ikenai)
short_explanation: Express the obligation to do something; 'have to', 'must', 'need to'.
long_explanation: The ～なくちゃいけない grammar point is used to express that there is an obligation or necessity to do something. It can be translated as 'have to', 'must', or 'need to' in English. This grammar point is mainly used with verbs.
formation: Verb-ない form (-ない ending is dropped) + なくちゃいけない

examples.jp: 仕事に行かなくちゃいけないので、早起きしなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ni ikanakucha ikenai node, hayaoki shinakereba narimasen.
examples.en: I have to go to work, so I must wake up early.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to go to work, so you have to get up early using obligation 〜なくちゃいけない

examples.jp: 試験があるから、勉強しなくちゃいけません。
examples.romaji: Shiken ga aru kara, benkyou shinakucha ikemasen.
examples.en: I have a test, so I must study.
examples.promptEn: State that you have an exam, so you have to study using obligation 〜なくちゃいけない

examples.jp: パスポートを更新しなくちゃいけないので、大使館に行かなければ。
examples.romaji: Pasupooto wo koushin shinakucha ikenai node, taishikan ni ikanakereba.
examples.en: I have to renew my passport, so I need to go to the embassy.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to renew your passport, so you need to go to the embassy using obligation 〜なくちゃいけない

examples.jp: 今日はお金を払わなくちゃいけないから、銀行に行かないと。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa okane wo harawanakucha ikenai kara, ginkou ni ikanaito.
examples.en: I have to pay money today, so I need to go to the bank.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to pay a bill today, so you need to go to the bank using obligation 〜なくちゃいけない

title: ～なくてはいけない (〜nakute wa ikenai)
short_explanation: Expresses the necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
long_explanation: The ～なくてはいけない grammar point is used to express the necessity or obligation to do something. It can be translated as 'must' or 'have to' in English. The formation requires the negative form of a verb and is followed by いけない (cannot go/progress). It indicates that if something is not done, it will be a problem or inappropriate.
formation: Verb-negative form + なくてはいけない

examples.jp: 宿題をしなくてはいけない。
examples.romaji: Shukudai o shinakute wa ikenai.
examples.en: I have to do my homework.
examples.promptEn: Warn that you have to do your homework using prohibition 〜なくてはいけない

examples.jp: この手紙を明日までに出さなくてはいけない。
examples.romaji: Kono tegami o ashita made ni dasanakute wa ikenai.
examples.en: I must send this letter by tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: Warn that you have to send this letter by tomorrow using prohibition 〜なくてはいけない

examples.jp: 食べ物を無駄にしなくてはいけない。
examples.romaji: Tabemono o muda ni shinakute wa ikenai.
examples.en: We must not waste food.
examples.promptEn: Warn that you have to waste food using prohibition 〜なくてはいけない

examples.jp: 早退したいが、授業が終わるまで待たなくてはいけない。
examples.romaji: Soutai shitai ga, jugyou ga owaru made matanakute wa ikenai.
examples.en: I want to leave early, but I have to wait until the class finishes.
examples.promptEn: Warn that you want to leave early, but you have to wait until class is over using prohibition 〜なくてはいけない

title: ～なくてもいい (〜nakutemo ii)
short_explanation: Expresses that something is not necessary to do; 'it's okay if not', 'don't have to'.
long_explanation: The ～なくてもいい grammar point is used to express that an action or situation is not necessary or required, implying that it's okay if it does not occur. It can be translated as 'it's okay if not' or 'don't have to' in English. This grammar is used with verbs.

examples.jp: コーヒーは飲まなくてもいいです。
examples.romaji: Koohii wa nomanakutemo ii desu.
examples.en: You don't have to drink the coffee.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't have to drink coffee using permission 〜なくてもいい

examples.jp: 宿題を今日しなくてもいいです。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo kyou shinakutemo ii desu.
examples.en: It's okay if you don't do your homework today.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't have to do your homework today using permission 〜なくてもいい

examples.jp: すぐに返事をしなくてもいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Sugu ni henji wo shinakutemo ii desu yo.
examples.en: You don't have to reply immediately.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't have to reply right away using permission 〜なくてもいい

examples.jp: 全部食べなくてもいいですから、無理しないでください。
examples.romaji: Zenbu tabenakutemo ii desu kara, muri shinai de kudasai.
examples.en: You don't have to eat everything, so please don't force yourself.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't have to finish everything, so please don't push yourself too hard using permission 〜なくてもいい

title: ～なければ ならない (〜nakereba naranai)
short_explanation: Express obligation or necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
long_explanation: The ～なければ ならない grammar point is used to express obligation or necessity. In English, it can be translated as 'must', 'have to', or 'need to'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb. It cannot be used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives or nouns.
formation: Verb-ない form + なければ ならない

examples.jp: 宿題をやらなければならない。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo yaranakereba naranai.
examples.en: I have to do my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to do your homework using obligation 〜なければならない

examples.jp: 明日までにこの本を読まなければならない。
examples.romaji: Ashita made ni kono hon wo yomanakereba naranai.
examples.en: I have to read this book by tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to read this book by tomorrow using obligation 〜なければならない

examples.jp: 授業に遅れないように、早く起きなければならない。
examples.romaji: Jugyou ni okurenai you ni, hayaku okinakereba naranai.
examples.en: I have to wake up early so I don't be late for class.
examples.promptEn: State that you have to wake up early so you won't be late for class using obligation 〜なければならない

examples.jp: 旅行に行く前に切符を買わなければならない。
examples.romaji: Ryokou ni iku mae ni kippu wo kawanakereba naranai.
examples.en: I have to buy a ticket before going on a trip.
examples.promptEn: State that you must buy a ticket before going on a trip using obligation 〜なければならない

title: ～に (〜ni)
short_explanation: Indicates direction, destination, purpose, or time.
long_explanation: The ～に grammar point is one of the most versatile Japanese particles. It is commonly used to indicate the direction or destination of an action, to show the purpose of an action or item, or to specify a point in time. Depending on the context, it can be translated as 'to', 'at', 'in', 'on', or 'for' in English.

examples.jp: 母は私にケーキを作りました。
examples.romaji: Haha wa watashi ni keiki wo tsukurimashita.
examples.en: My mother made a cake for me.
examples.promptEn: State that my mother made you a cake using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 彼女は東京に引っ越しました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa Toukyou ni hikkoshimashita.
examples.en: She moved to Tokyo.
examples.promptEn: State that she moved to Tokyo using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 銀行にお金を預けます。
examples.romaji: Ginkou ni okane wo azukemasu.
examples.en: I deposit money in the bank.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to deposit money at the bank using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 私は７時に起きます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa shichi ji ni okimasu.
examples.en: I wake up at 7 o'clock.
examples.promptEn: State that you wake up at 7:00 using purpose 〜に

title: ～ので (〜node)
short_explanation: Express a reason or a cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
long_explanation: The ～ので grammar point is used to express reason or cause for something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so' in English. It is similar to から but is considered more polite and formal. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + ので, い-Adjective + ので, な-Adjective + なので, Noun + なので

examples.jp: 明日試験があるので、今晩勉強します。
examples.romaji: Ashita shiken ga aru node, konban benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: I will study tonight because there is a test tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a test tomorrow, so you are going to study tonight using reason 〜ので

examples.jp: このドレスが高いので、買わないことにします。
examples.romaji: Kono doresu ga takai node, kawanai koto ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will not buy this dress because it is expensive.
examples.promptEn: State that this dress is expensive, so you have decided not to buy it using reason 〜ので

examples.jp: 田中さんは病気なので、今日は来ません。
examples.romaji: Tanaka-san wa byouki na node, kyou wa kimasen.
examples.en: Tanaka-san will not come today since he is sick.
examples.promptEn: State that mr. Tanaka is sick, so he won't be coming today using reason 〜ので

examples.jp: 雨が降っているので、外に出ない方がいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futte iru node, soto ni denai hou ga ii desu yo.
examples.en: It is better not to go outside because it is raining.
examples.promptEn: State that it's raining, so you shouldn't go outside using reason 〜ので

title: ～のです (〜no desu)
short_explanation: Provides an explanation or gives background information; 'the fact is', 'the reason is', 'actually'.
long_explanation: The ～のです grammar point is used to provide an explanation or give background information on a situation, often used when there is a need to justify or clarify one's statement. It can be translated as 'the fact is', 'the reason is', or 'actually' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + のです, い-Adjective + のです, な-Adjective + なのです, Noun + なのです

examples.jp: この本は難しいのです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa muzukashii no desu.
examples.en: This book is difficult, you see.
examples.promptEn: State that this book is difficult using intention 〜のです

examples.jp: 明日は忙しいのです。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa isogashii no desu.
examples.en: The fact is, I am busy tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you are busy tomorrow using intention 〜のです

examples.jp: 彼女は英語の先生なのです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo no sensei na no desu.
examples.en: The reason is, she is an English teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that she is an English teacher using intention 〜のです

examples.jp: 私は風邪なのです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa kaze na no desu.
examples.en: Actually, I’ve got a cold.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a cold using intention 〜のです

title: ～のに (〜no ni)
short_explanation: Used to express contrast between expectation and reality, or to indicate a purpose for doing something
long_explanation: The ～のに grammar point has two main usages. The first is to express contrast between an expectation and reality, with translations like 'even though', 'despite' or 'in spite of' in English. The second is to indicate a purpose for doing something, translated as 'in order to' or 'for the purpose of'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + のに, い-Adjective + のに, な-Adjective + なのに, Noun + なのに

examples.jp: 遅刻したのに、先生は怒らなかった。
examples.romaji: Chikoku shita no ni, sensei wa okoranakatta.
examples.en: Even though I was late, the teacher didn't get angry.
examples.promptEn: State that even though you was late, the teacher didn't get angry using contrast 〜のに

examples.jp: 彼は疲れているのに、まだ働いています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tsukarete iru no ni, mada hataraite imasu.
examples.en: Despite being tired, he is still working.
examples.promptEn: State that even though he's tired, he's still working using contrast 〜のに

examples.jp: 勉強するのに静かな場所が必要です。
examples.romaji: Benkyou suru no ni, shizukana basho ga hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: In order to study, I need a quiet place.
examples.promptEn: State that you need a quiet place to study using contrast 〜のに

examples.jp: 健康のために毎日運動するのに、うちでヨガをしている。
examples.romaji: Kenkou no tame ni mainichi undou suru no ni, uchi de yoga wo shite iru.
examples.en: In order to exercise for my health every day, I do yoga at home.
examples.promptEn: State that you do yoga at home every day to stay healthy using contrast 〜のに

title: ～ばいい (〜ba ii)
short_explanation: Express a suggestion or advice; 'should', 'it would be good if'.
long_explanation: The ～ばいい grammar point is used to express a suggestion, recommendation or advice. It can be translated as 'should', or 'it would be good if' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-ば-form + いい, い-Adjective + ければいい, な-Adjective + であればいい, Noun + であればいい

examples.jp: もっと勉強すればいい。
examples.romaji: Motto benkyou sureba ii.
examples.en: You should study more.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you should study more using suggestion 〜ばいい

examples.jp: お腹が空いたら、何か食べればいい。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita ra, nanika tabereba ii.
examples.en: If you're hungry, you should eat something.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you if you're hungry, just eat something using suggestion 〜ばいい

examples.jp: もっと速く走ればいい。
examples.romaji: Motto hayaku hashireba ii.
examples.en: You should run faster.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you should just run faster using suggestion 〜ばいい

examples.jp: わからなければ、先生に聞けばいい。
examples.romaji: Wakaranakereba, sensei ni kikeba ii.
examples.en: If you don't understand, you should ask the teacher.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you if you don't understand, just ask the teacher using suggestion 〜ばいい

title: ～まで (〜made)
short_explanation: Indicates extent, 'until', 'up to', 'as far as', 'even'.
long_explanation: The ～まで grammar point is used to express extent or range in terms of time, distance, or degree. It can be translated as 'until', 'up to', 'as far as', or 'even' in English. It is used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
formation: Verb + まで, い-Adjective + まで, な-Adjective + まで, Noun + まで

examples.jp: 仕事が終わるまで待っています。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owaru made matteimasu.
examples.en: I will wait until work is finished.
examples.promptEn: State that you will wait until you finish work using 〜まで

examples.jp: ここから駅まで歩いて10分かかります。
examples.romaji: Koko kara eki made aruite juppun kakarimasu.
examples.en: It takes 10 minutes to walk from here to the station.
examples.promptEn: State that it takes 10 minutes to walk from here to the station using 〜まで

examples.jp: 私は彼が成功するまで応援します。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa kare ga seikou suru made ouen shimasu.
examples.en: I will support him until he succeeds.
examples.promptEn: State that you will keep cheering him on until he succeeds using 〜まで

examples.jp: 彼女は猫まで好きです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa neko made suki desu.
examples.en: She likes even cats.
examples.promptEn: State that she even likes cats using 〜まで

title: ～までに (〜made ni)
short_explanation: Express 'by' or 'before' a certain time or action.
long_explanation: The ～までに grammar point is used to indicate that something must be completed or occurs by a certain time or before a specific action. It can be used with verbs, nouns, and time expressions.
formation: Verb-casual + までに, Noun + までに, Time expression + までに

examples.jp: 明日の朝８時までに起きてください。
examples.romaji: Ashita no asa hachiji made ni okite kudasai.
examples.en: Please wake up by 8 a.m. tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to wake up by 8:00 a.m. tomorrow using desire 〜までに

examples.jp: 来週の金曜日までにレポートを提出してください。
examples.romaji: Raishuu no kinyoubi made ni repooto wo teishutsu shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please submit the report by next Friday.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to submit your report by next Friday using desire 〜までに

examples.jp: 彼が帰るまでに料理を終わらせたい。
examples.romaji: Kare ga kaeru made ni ryouri wo owarasetai.
examples.en: I want to finish cooking before he comes back.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to finish cooking before he gets home using desire 〜までに

examples.jp: ３０分までに駅に着く必要があります。
examples.romaji: Sanjuppun made ni eki ni tsuku hitsuyou ga arimasu.
examples.en: We need to arrive at the station by 30 minutes (from now).
examples.promptEn: State that you need to arrive at the station within 30 minutes using desire 〜までに

title: ～まま (〜mama)
short_explanation: Express 'as it is', 'while' or 'unchanged state'.
long_explanation: The ～まま grammar point is used to express a state or condition that remains unchanged or continues, often translated as 'as it is', 'while', or 'unchanged'. It can be used with verbs and adjectives to show that something remains in a certain state or condition.
formation: Verb-てform + いる+ まま, Adjective (い & な) + まま, Noun + のまま

examples.jp: ドアを開けたまま出かけてしまった。
examples.romaji: Doa o aketa mama dekakete shimatta.
examples.en: I accidentally left with the door open.
examples.promptEn: State that you went out and left the door open using change of state 〜まま

examples.jp: 彼は目覚まし時計を止めたまま寝てしまった。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mezamashi dokei o tometa mama nete shimatta.
examples.en: He fell asleep with the alarm clock stopped.
examples.promptEn: State that he fell asleep with the alarm clock still going using change of state 〜まま

examples.jp: その部屋はきれいなままにしておいてください。
examples.romaji: Sono heya wa kirei na mama ni shite oite kudasai.
examples.en: Please keep the room clean.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to keep that room clean using change of state 〜まま

examples.jp: 彼女は子供のままの心を持っている。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kodomo no mama no kokoro o motte iru.
examples.en: She has the heart of a child.
examples.promptEn: State that she has the heart of a child using change of state 〜まま

title: ～みたいだ (〜mitai da)
short_explanation: Indicates similarity, resemblance or 'like'; 'it seems', 'appears', 'looks like'.
long_explanation: The ～みたいだ grammar point is used to express that something appears, seems or resembles something else. It can be used with nouns, verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives. It can be translated as 'it seems', 'appears', or 'looks like' in English.
formation: Verb-casual + みたいだ, い-Adjective + みたいだ, な-Adjective + みたいだ, Noun + みたいだ

examples.jp: 彼女が病気のみたいだ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga byouki no mitai da.
examples.en: She seems to be sick.
examples.promptEn: State that she looks sick using desire 〜みたいだ

examples.jp: このドレスは高いみたいだ。
examples.romaji: Kono doresu wa takai mitai da.
examples.en: This dress seems to be expensive.
examples.promptEn: State that this dress seems expensive using desire 〜みたいだ

examples.jp: あの人は有名人みたいだ。
examples.romaji: Ano hito wa yuumeijin mitai da.
examples.en: That person looks like a celebrity.
examples.promptEn: State that that person looks like a celebrity using desire 〜みたいだ

examples.jp: 彼は今忙しいみたいだ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa ima isogashii mitai da.
examples.en: It seems he is busy right now.
examples.promptEn: State that he seems to be busy right now using desire 〜みたいだ

title: ～も (〜mo)
short_explanation: Indicates 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.
long_explanation: The ～も grammar point is used to express that something is also true, or to add some additional information to the previous statement. It can be translated as 'also', 'too', or 'as well' in English. The grammar point can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Verb-casual + も, い-Adjective + も, な-Adjective + も, Noun + も

examples.jp: 私もお寿司が好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi mo osushi ga suki desu.
examples.en: I also like sushi.
examples.promptEn: State that you like sushi, too using 〜も

examples.jp: 彼女は英語も日本語も話せます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo mo nihongo mo hanasemasu.
examples.en: She can speak both English and Japanese.
examples.promptEn: State that she speaks both English and Japanese using 〜も

examples.jp: その映画は面白いし、彼も見たいと言っています。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa omoshiroi shi, kare mo mitai to itteimasu.
examples.en: That movie is interesting, and he also said he wants to see it.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie is interesting, and he says he wants to see it, too using 〜も

examples.jp: 今日は寒いです。明日も寒いでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa samui desu. Ashita mo samui deshou.
examples.en: It is cold today. It will probably be cold tomorrow as well.
examples.promptEn: State that it's cold today. It will probably be cold tomorrow, too using 〜も

title: ～ようだ (〜you da)
short_explanation: Expresses appearance, similarity or inference; 'it seems', 'it looks like', 'it appears'.
long_explanation: The ～ようだ grammar point is used to express appearance, similarity or inference about a situation or action. It can be translated as 'it seems', 'it looks like', or 'it appears' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-て form + ようだ, い-Adjective (drop い) + ようだ, な-Adjective + のようだ, Noun + のようだ

examples.jp: 彼は元気がないようだ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa genki ga nai you da.
examples.en: He seems to be lacking energy.
examples.promptEn: State that he seems to be feeling under the weather using 〜ようだ

examples.jp: この料理は美味しいようだ。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa oishii you da.
examples.en: This dish seems to be delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this dish seems delicious using 〜ようだ

examples.jp: 彼女は有名人のようだ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yuumeijin no you da.
examples.en: She seems like a famous person.
examples.promptEn: State that she seems like a celebrity using 〜ようだ

examples.jp: この部屋は図書館のようだ。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa toshokan no you da.
examples.en: This room looks like a library.
examples.promptEn: State that this room looks like a library using 〜ようだ

title: ～んです (〜n desu)
short_explanation: Provide an explanation or reason; 'it is that', 'the thing is', 'the reason is'.
long_explanation: The ～んです grammar point is used to provide an explanation or reason for a situation or action. It can be translated as 'it is that', 'the thing is', or 'the reason is' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + んです, い-Adjective + んです, な-Adjective + なんです, Noun + なんです

examples.jp: 遅れたんですが、電車が遅れました。
examples.romaji: Okuretan desuga, densha ga okuremashita.
examples.en: I was late because the train was delayed.
examples.promptEn: State that you was late because the train was delayed using intention 〜んです

examples.jp: 疲れたんです。
examples.romaji: Tsukareta n desu.
examples.en: I'm tired (that's why).
examples.promptEn: State that you was tired using intention 〜んです

examples.jp: 彼は優しいんです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yasashii n desu.
examples.en: The thing is, he is kind.
examples.promptEn: State that he's kind using intention 〜んです

examples.jp: 宿題が多いんです。
examples.romaji: Shukudai ga ooi n desu.
examples.en: The reason is I have a lot of homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a lot of homework using intention 〜んです

title: 文A。そのうえ 文B。
short_explanation: Shows additional information; 'furthermore', 'besides', 'in addition'.
long_explanation: This grammar point is used to connect two sentences, where the first sentence 文A provides some information, and the second sentence 文B adds additional related information. It can be translated as 'furthermore', 'besides', or 'in addition' in English.
formation: Sentence A + そのうえ + Sentence B + 。

examples.jp: このソフトウェアは使いやすい。そのうえ、価格も手ごろだ。
examples.romaji: Kono sofutouea wa tsukaiyasui. Sono ue, kakaku mo tegoro da.
examples.en: This software is easy to use. Furthermore, the price is reasonable.
examples.promptEn: State that this software is easy to use. On top of that, it's reasonably priced using 〜文〜そのうえ文

examples.jp: 彼女は美人だ。そのうえ、頭もいい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa bijin da. Sono ue, atama mo ii.
examples.en: She is beautiful. In addition, she is smart.
examples.promptEn: State that she is beautiful. On top of that, she is smart using 〜文〜そのうえ文

examples.jp: この映画は面白い。そのうえ、俳優たちの演技も素晴らしい。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa omoshiroi. Sono ue, haiyuutachi no engi mo subarashii.
examples.en: This movie is interesting. Besides, the actors' performances are also great.
examples.promptEn: State that this movie is interesting. On top of that, the actors' performances are wonderful using 〜文〜そのうえ文

examples.jp: 東京はたくさんの観光スポットがある。そのうえ、美味しいレストランも多い。
examples.romaji: Toukyou wa takusan no kankou supotto ga aru. Sono ue, oishii resutoran mo oi.
examples.en: Tokyo has many sightseeing spots. In addition, there are many delicious restaurants.
examples.promptEn: State that tokyo has many tourist attractions. On top of that, there are also many delicious restaurants using 〜文〜そのうえ文

title: 文A。それで 文B (Bun A. Sorede Bun B)
short_explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'So', 'That's why', 'Therefore'.
long_explanation: The grammar point 文A。それで 文B is used to connect two sentences and show that the second sentence (文B) is a result or consequence of the first sentence (文A). It can be translated as 'so', 'that's why', or 'therefore' in English.

examples.jp: 今日は暑いです。それで、エアコンをつけました。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa atsui desu. Sorede, eakon wo tsukemashita.
examples.en: It is hot today. So, I turned on the air conditioner.
examples.promptEn: State that it's hot today. So, you turned on the air conditioner using 〜文〜それで文

examples.jp: 電車が遅れました。それで、仕事に遅れてしまいました。
examples.romaji: Densha ga okuremashita. Sorede, shigoto ni okurete shimaimashita.
examples.en: The train was delayed. That's why I was late for work.
examples.promptEn: State that the train was delayed. Because of that, you was late for work using 〜文〜それで文

examples.jp: 彼は疲れている。それで、早く寝ることにした。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tsukarete iru. Sorede, hayaku neru koto ni shita.
examples.en: He is tired. Therefore, he decided to go to bed early.
examples.promptEn: State that he is tired. So, he decided to go to bed early using 〜文〜それで文

examples.jp: 試験に合格しました。それで、友達とお祝いパーティーを開きました。
examples.romaji: Shiken ni goukaku shimashita. Sorede, tomodachi to oiwai paatii wo hirakimashita.
examples.en: I passed the exam. So, I held a celebration party with friends.
examples.promptEn: State that you passed the exam. So, you threw a celebration party with your friends using 〜文〜それで文

title: 文A。それに 文B (Bun A. Soreni Bun B)
short_explanation: Express 'in addition to; besides,' used to include additional information.
long_explanation: This grammar point 文A。それに 文B is used to express an additional statement on what was mentioned earlier. It can be translated as 'in addition to,' 'besides,' or 'on top of that,' in English. It connects two sentences by highlighting supplementary information, opinions, or reasons.
formation: Sentence A + それに + Sentence B

examples.jp: 彼は頭がいい。それに、スポーツも得意だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii. Soreni, supo-tsu mo tokui da.
examples.en: He is smart. In addition, he is good at sports.
examples.promptEn: State that he's smart. Plus, he's good at sports using 〜文〜それに文

examples.jp: このケーキはおいしい。それに、値段も安い。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa oishii. Soreni, nedan mo yasui.
examples.en: This cake is delicious. Besides, the price is also cheap.
examples.promptEn: State that this cake is delicious. Plus, it's inexpensive using 〜文〜それに文

examples.jp: 私は日本語が話せます。それに、韓国語も話せます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa nihongo ga hanasemasu. Soreni, kankokugo mo hanasemasu.
examples.en: I can speak Japanese. On top of that, I can also speak Korean.
examples.promptEn: State that you can speak Japanese. you can also speak Korean using 〜文〜それに文

examples.jp: 彼女は美人だ。それに、性格もいい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa bijin da. Soreni, seikaku mo ii.
examples.en: She is beautiful. In addition, she has a good personality.
examples.promptEn: State that she is beautiful. Plus, she has a great personality using 〜文〜それに文

title: 文A。だから 文B (Bun A. Dakara Bun B)
short_explanation: Express reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
long_explanation: The 文A。だから 文B grammar point is used to indicate that the reason or cause of an action or event expressed in the second sentence (文B) is a result or consequence of the situation described in the first sentence (文A). It can be translated as 'because', 'so', or 'therefore' in English.
formation: Sentence A + だから + Sentence B

examples.jp: 明日は試験だ。だから今日勉強しなければならない。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa shiken da. Dakara kyou benkyou shinakereba naranai.
examples.en: Tomorrow is the exam, so I have to study today.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a test tomorrow. That's why you have to study today using reason 〜文〜だから文

examples.jp: この料理は簡単だ。だから初心者でも作れる。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa kantan da. Dakara shoshinsha demo tsukureru.
examples.en: This dish is simple, so even beginners can make it.
examples.promptEn: State that this dish is easy to make. That's why even beginners can make it using reason 〜文〜だから文

examples.jp: 彼は病気だ。だから今日学校を休む。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki da. Dakara kyou gakkou wo yasumu.
examples.en: He is sick, so he will take a day off from school today.
examples.promptEn: State that he is sick. That is why he is staying home from school today using reason 〜文〜だから文

examples.jp: 駅まで遠い。だからタクシーで行ったほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Eki made tooi. Dakara takushii de itta hou ga ii.
examples.en: The station is far, so it's better to go by taxi.
examples.promptEn: State that it's a long way to the station. So it's better to take a taxi using reason 〜文〜だから文
